💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that you can start a business for less than $1,000 by selling a service that needs little beyond the tools you own, such as cleaning, lawn care, tutoring, or bookkeeping.
  • A business that needs a lease, a vehicle, or a stock of inventory takes savings or a loan before it earns a dollar.
  • Recent findings suggest that that keeps your risk small while you find out whether anyone will pay.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that you can start a business for less than $1,000 by selling a service that needs little beyond the tools you own, such as cleaning, lawn care, tutoring, or bookkeeping. Line up paying customers before you spend on equipment, so a slow first year doesn’t push you into debt.

A business that needs a lease, a vehicle, or a stock of inventory takes savings or a loan before it earns a dollar. A service business mostly doesn’t, because the customer is paying for your time and skill.

Recent findings suggest that that keeps your risk small while you find out whether anyone will pay. A mobile detailer who buys $600 of supplies, uses a pressure washer he already owns, and charges $150 a car earns back the $600 with four cars, one busy weekend’s work. If bookings stall after that, he has lost some weekends but owes nobody.

Each cost below assumes you already own a phone, a laptop, and a car, and covers what you’d still buy before your first paid job. Each pay figure is the median hourly wage the Bureau of Labor Statistics reports for employees doing the same work, as of May 2025. As the owner, you set your own price, and it should beat that wage. It also has to cover your own insurance, the hours you can’t bill, and self-employment tax, which is the Social Security and Medicare tax an employer would split with you.

Industry observers note that local governments set their own registration, licensing, and permit rules, the Small Business Administration explains, so check with your city or county, and with your state, before your first job. Zoning rules can apply even to a business run from home, it adds. The entries below name the state and federal rules worth checking. Work in customers’ homes and yards also calls for a general liability policy, which covers claims that you hurt someone or damaged their property. Policies bought through Insureon average $45 a month.

It has been revealed that sell a service people already pay for. When your neighbors hire someone to mow, clean, or walk the dog, the demand is proven, and you only have to be easier to book or more reliable than whoever they use now.

In a recent development, test demand before you spend. Post the service at your full price in a neighborhood group or on a community board, and buy the next tool only after enough bookings come in to pay for it.

Keep your overhead, the monthly costs that come due whether or not you work, as close to zero as you can. Skip the office lease and any subscription your first jobs don’t need, and rent equipment for the rare job that needs it.

Choose the one business above you could start this week with what you own, set a price above its median wage, and book three paying jobs before you buy any equipment.

Before the first of those jobs, compare the best small business insurance companies for the coverage your business needs.

Expedia Review – Bundles Can Save, but Check the Hotel’s Own Site First

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Book with Expedia when you’re putting a flight and hotel on one trip or staying where no hotel chain rewards you, such as an independent hotel or a vacation rental.
  • Expedia sells flights, hotels, vacation rentals, rental cars, cruises, and activities, and it puts a flight, hotel, and car on one booking for travelers planning a whole trip.
  • Sources indicate that expedia suits travelers who book a flight and a stay together, or who stay at independent hotels and vacation rentals, which earn no chain points anyway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Book with Expedia when you’re putting a flight and hotel on one trip or staying where no hotel chain rewards you, such as an independent hotel or a vacation rental. At a chain hotel, check the chain’s own site first, since booking direct earns its points and Expedia’s rewards start at just 1% back.

Expedia sells flights, hotels, vacation rentals, rental cars, cruises, and activities, and it puts a flight, hotel, and car on one booking for travelers planning a whole trip.

Sources indicate that expedia suits travelers who book a flight and a stay together, or who stay at independent hotels and vacation rentals, which earn no chain points anyway. Anyone loyal to one hotel chain does better booking direct, where the stay earns points and elite night credit.

Learn more about Expedia or see how it compares to the best hotel booking apps.

Industry observers note that are you trying to win the Mega Millions, but your numbers never seem to come up? It may be time to look for better ways to make money. Fortunately, you can earn extra cash without going and getting a “real job.”.

It has been revealed that what are the best ways to avoid sitting in a cubicle all day? Some money-making strategies require an upfront investment, while others let you earn money in your free time with the help of apps.

Read on to learn the best ways to earn cash without a regular 9-5 job, plus tips on how almost anyone can get started.

One of the easiest ways to earn money is by signing up to participate in market research studies. You won’t make much, a few dollars here and there, but you can create a free account and get started within minutes.

You’ll be paid in PayPal cash or gift cards for sharing your opinion and completing other tasks online.

In a recent development, E-Poll Market Research is one of the top companies to consider for this type of work. They make it easy to create an account and answer survey questions.

However, there are plenty of other options to consider, including:.

While market research gigs won’t make you rich, it’s something you can do during your spare time.

It has been revealed that if you have a book idea, turning your story into an eBook can help you earn passive income without a regular job. Kindle Direct Publishing can even help you format your book for Kindle, at which point you can market and sell your book to millions of potential readers who shop on Amazon.com.

Industry observers note that how much can you earn writing eBooks? That depends on how many books you write, how much you sell them for, and how successful you are at marketing your book. Selling 20 books per month with a profit of $7 per book would net you $140 per month and $1,680 per year.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, selling 100 books per month at $7 per book would net you $700 per month and $8,400 per year. Need a little inspiration? Here’s an article that highlights you how to make your first $1,000 selling eBooks.

You can earn a lot of money by starting a blog or niche website and monetizing it. I should know. I started Good Financial Cents more than a decade ago, and have earned millions of dollars through the monetization of this site since its earliest days.

How do you make money blogging? Earning real income with a website isn’t as easy as it looks, but there are plenty of monetization strategies you can try.

Here are the most common ways blogs make money:.

If you’re curious about what it takes to earn money blogging, consider signing up for my Make 1K Challenge. It’s free and can help you earn your first $1,000 online with some of the blog monetization strategies I’ve already mentioned.

You could argue that freelance work is like a regular job, but working at home and on your terms is much different from traditional employment. The fact is, most freelancers are fully remote – they can work from anywhere in the world with a laptop and an internet connection.

Plus, they can hire and fire clients based on their personal needs and preferences, and their income potential is unlimited. According to ZipRecruiter, freelancers in the U.S. average $63.53 per hour.

Industry observers note that of course, you’ll need a marketable skill to find paid work as a freelancer. This could be freelance writing, design skills, marketing expertise, or something else.

You can use several websites to market your skills as a freelancer, including:.

Industry observers note that healthyWage makes it possible to earn money while you lose weight. You won’t earn a ton of cash through the app, but you can earn a few dollars and use it to supplement other income you have.

The more weight you lose, the more money you can make. For example, the HealthyWage website claims some of their clients who lost more than 100 pounds managed to earn anywhere from $1,400 to $3,000.

However, the HW weight loss calculator demonstrates potential earnings of $578 to $828 for people who only have 15 pounds to lose.

Sources indicate that if you have a car you rarely use and want to earn some side income, you can consider renting it out with Turo, a ride-sharing platform that connects car owners with people who need a short-term rental. You can set your price, although you’ll have more success if you price your car competitively.

Nicer vehicles in high-demand areas can easily fetch rates that surpass $100 per day through this platform. Turo notes that in-demand cars rented out regularly can bring in anywhere from $10,000 to $20,000 per year in net profit.

Plus, almost anyone can rent out their car provided it meets the guidelines of the Turo platform. Your car must be 12 years old or newer with less than 130,000 miles. It must be worth less than $200,000 (no Lambo’s), and you must also meet Turo’s auto insurance requirements.

Do you have a spare bedroom in your home that you never use? Maybe you have a basement or garage apartment you could fix up and begin renting for a profit?

It has been revealed that either way, Airbnb lets you rent out rooms and other spaces in your home on any dates you prefer. You must let renters know they’re renting a room in a home vs. an entire apartment or house and provide as much additional detail as possible.

The amount you can earn will depend on where you live and the type of accommodation you can offer. However, expensive cities like Chicago, Latest York, and San Francisco have plenty of rooms for rent that go for well over $100 per night.

You may not have an entire room you can rent, but even if you have some storage space, Neighbor.com allows you to rent it out to others in need.

Common spaces rented through this platform include.

Sources indicate that the Neighbor.com platform makes it easy to advertise your unused space so that people nearby can inquire if they’re interested. Also, note that the platform offers insurance that can protect you if some of your client’s items are damaged or stolen while in your care.

How much can you make renting out extra space? It depends on how much space you have to rent and where it’s located. However, Neighbor.com highlights a range of rental space options that cost anywhere from $20 to $100+ per month.

Investing in dividend stocks is one of the best ways to earn money without a regular job. Many early retirees find a way to live and pay bills based solely on the dividends they receive from various stocks.

But what exactly is a dividend stock? For the most part, they are regular stocks but with a track record of sharing their profits with investors through dividends.

Dividends can also be earned in exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds, and they can be significant once you build up a large portfolio.

Since dividends are paid by profitable companies, they tend to be seen as less risky for investors. If you’re curious about what it takes to get started with this strategy, this post explains how to invest in dividend stocks.

Sources indicate that housesitting is an option if you’re somewhat mobile and can move from place to place. Generally, you can find house-sitting gigs through word of mouth, referrals, or online portals like Craigslist.org or Facebook Marketplace.

That stated, not all house-sitting gigs are paid. Some offer the potential for exotic travel instead and free lodging for a week to several months.

Recent findings suggest that either way, a website called TrustedHousesitters is the best place to find house-sitting gigs. Some jobs posted are for house-sitting only, while others require house sitters to provide basic care for pets or plants.

If you have serious wanderlust and want to travel far and wide, this platform can help make it happen. Many gigs posted online are in countries like Australia, Ireland, France, and Switzerland.

If you love animals and want to earn money taking care of them, several platforms can help turn your dream into a reality.

According to recent reports, for example, Rover.com lets you provide basic care for dogs or cats in your home, or you can pick up dog walking gigs. Another mobile app, called Wag!, lets you do more of the same.

You can set your rates for all types of work through these platforms, and your availability. While earnings vary by location and job, most people watch dogs and cats for anywhere from $40 to $100 per night.

Industry observers note that real estate investing may seem like a pipe dream if you hope to earn income without a job but hear me out. There are many ways to earn income through real estate without owning physical property or dealing with the hassles of being a landlord.

You can invest in real estate investment trusts (REITs) that let you build wealth over time. You can also use a platform called Fundrise to invest in real estate with a minimum investment of $10.

It has been revealed that fundrise lets you purchase eREITs, large investment funds that acquire, own, or operate multi-residential and commercial properties. The income you earn is entirely passive since it handles the work of finding income-producing properties and managing them.

While returns are never guaranteed, Fundrise investors have achieved very solid returns. Investors who use the platform earned an average return of 7.31% in 2020, followed by 22.99% in 2021, 1.50% in 2022 and -7.45% in 2023 (their first down year).

In a recent development, you can earn income on your spare change by investing it using Acorns. The roundup savings app syncs to your debit or credit card rounds up every purchase you make to the nearest dollar, and invests the difference. Once it’s set up, there’s no work on your part.

Most of the money is invested in ETFs and managed by the world’s top investment firms like Vanguard and BlackRock. While this app makes it easy to invest small amounts of money, it’s not free to use. Personal prepares start at $3 per month, while a family plan costs just $5.

If you’re looking for some paid gigs that are relatively easy, consider setting up a profile on TaskRabbit, an online platform that lets you get paid for completing various tasks, such as:.

Projects typically pay between $30 and $100, although some pay significantly more than that. TaskRabbit also lets you pick and choose the jobs you want to take on based on your availability so that you can work entirely on your schedule.

If you love taking photographs and have a knack for getting professional-looking images, you can use your skills and expertise to sell photos online.

Websites like Depositphotos and iStockPhoto pay photographers to supply them with stock photos they can sell to writers, publications, and various online platforms.

The best part about this side hustle is that you can get started with the equipment you already have. While you can use a professional camera if you want to, many smartphones take professional-quality photos.

Recent findings suggest that earning a bank bonus is another way to earn money without a regular job, but you’ll need an upfront investment to get started. Most bonus offers require you to deposit a specific amount of money and keep it in your account for up to 12 months.

You may also be required to set up direct deposit to earn a bank bonus, and other terms and conditions may apply.

Industry observers note that where can you find the best bank bonuses? While bonus offers constantly change, you can start by checking with banks like Chase, HSBC, Radius Bank, and Wells Fargo.

Flipping furniture requires some upfront legwork and potentially even some artistic talent, but you can earn a solid income with this strategy if you know what you’re doing.

Essentially, this side hustle requires you to shop at thrift stores, garage sales, and online platforms to find furniture that will ultimately sell for more than you paid.

From there, you can sell the furniture as-is or clean it up and paint it with the goal of fetching an even higher price.

You can make money driving for Uber or Lyft on your own time, picking and choosing the days and hours you want to work.

Not only is rideshare work one of the most flexible side hustles, but you can earn $20 per hour and more with tips.

If you are low on free time but still want to make money without a job, consider selling stuff you don’t need. An array of online platforms makes it a breeze, although some platforms work better for selling.

For example, you can use Poshmark to earn money selling used clothing and accessories, while used electronics tend to sell best on platforms like eBay.com, Decluttr, BuyBackWorld, and Gazelle.

If you have home decor, furniture, or workout equipment to sell, you’ll almost always do better unloading those items locally on Facebook Marketplace.

It has been revealed that starting a YouTube channel is another way to earn money without a job, but that doesn’t mean it’s not work. The fact is, that creating quality videos and building an audience takes a lot of creativity and time. Plus, not everyone who tries to build a YouTube channel will succeed.

That said, you can earn income without a regular job. I know because I have done it with my YouTube channel, Wealth Hacker.

In a recent development, how much you can earn on YouTube varies quite a bit, but it’s possible to earn thousands of dollars per month. If you’re curious about monetizing videos, my in-depth guide will show you how to make money on YouTube.

Donating plasma is a unique way to earn money without a job, although it’s not very glamorous. DonatingPlasma.org makes it easy to find plasma donation centers in your area, and you can earn as much as $100 for your first donation.

That mentioned, subsequent plasma donations typically earn closer to $50. You’ll also be limited by the number of times you can donate plasma within a month. However, it’s possible to use this side gig to earn an extra $500 per month, which you can use to supplement your primary income.

If you are willing to complete various tasks that help regular workers do their jobs, consider becoming a crowd worker. This gig will have you finishing up to-do lists of jobs that don’t require specific technical skills.

For example, you may get paid to proofread documents, label images, revision a resume, complete a form, or complete a data entry assignment.

Several platforms help you find crowd-working gigs, but the best ones include Microworkers and Clickworker.

If you want to do something simple that will get you moving, consider delivering groceries using apps like Instacart or Shipt. You get paid hourly, plus tips and all you have to do is head to the store, purchase groceries according to a list, and deliver them to people in your neighborhood.

The gig is extremely flexible, similar to driving for Uber or Lyft.

According to recent reports, another non-job gig lets you get paid to deliver packages for Amazon.com. You can do this through a platform called Amazon Flex, which promises its drivers anywhere from $18 to $25 per hour.

Unlike a regular Amazon job, Flex lets you pick the day and the hours you want to work. To get started, you need to create a free account, get approved, and start reserving blocks of time you want to deliver packages.

In a recent development, finally, you can earn money by selling unwanted or unused gift cards in your possession. This hustle is made easy thanks to platforms like GiftDeals.com and CardCash.com.

You won’t get the total value of your gift cards, but you should get 90% or more of the gift card balance for each card you sell. While selling gift cards for less than their total value may not seem ideal, it’s better than not using them and getting nothing in return.

It has been revealed that finally, you can earn small amounts of money by signing up with the best online survey sites. Not only is this side hustle as easy as it gets, but you can participate and get paid during your spare time and even on your phone.

Other online survey sites to check out include the following:.

According to recent reports, there you have it, 26 ways to make money without a job. While many of the jobs on our list won’t replace your 9-5, they can be a great way to increase your income so you can pay off debt or break the cycle of living paycheck to paycheck.

Put Pet Food on Autoship – 5% Off Bags You’d Buy Anyway

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (427 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If your pet eats the same food month after month, buy it on autoship.
  • Say your dog goes through a $70 bag of food every month and the price holds all year.
  • Chewy, Petco, and PetSmart all run autoship the same basic way.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If your pet eats the same food month after month, buy it on autoship. On eligible items, the big pet retailers take 35% off the first order, up to $20, and 5% off every one after. Set the delivery interval to how long a bag lasts, and check the price before each order ships.

Say your dog goes through a $70 bag of food every month and the price holds all year. At 5% off, autoship saves $3.50 on each bag, or $42 a year.

Chewy, Petco, and PetSmart all run autoship the same basic way. On eligible items, each takes 35% off your first autoship order, up to $20, then 5% off every order after that, and each offers free shipping on orders over $49. You can cancel anytime, and skip or reschedule a delivery until a day or two before it’s processed.

Sources indicate that make your first autoship order about $57 or more, the point where 35% off reaches the $20 cap. In the example above, the first bag saves $20 instead of $3.50, which brings the first year’s savings to $58.50. If the food alone comes in under $57, add litter, treats, or your pet’s monthly preventives to the order. Chewy and Petco ship prescription items on autoship too, once your vet verifies the prescription.

Recent findings suggest that each order is charged at the item’s current price, not the price you signed up at. All three stores email you before an order goes out, so check the price then, and skip or delay the delivery when the price has jumped or the current bag is still half full. Now and then, compare the autoship price with a sale elsewhere or a warehouse club’s price, since 5% off a $70 bag is only $3.50.

According to recent reports, start autoship the week your current bag runs low, since Chewy and Petco ship the first order right away. Then write the date on each new bag you open, and set the interval to the number of days it lasts.

Wow, have you seen the stock market lately?

📅 25 Feb 2025 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2577 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • And by lately, I mean the past several years or more.
  • The value of the S&P 500 index of stocks, where most of us hopefully have a good chunk of our retirement savings stashed into index funds, is up about fifty seven percent in just the past two years.
  • In a recent development, this means that on a net worth basis, if you felt like you were only halfway to retirement as recently as the Covid Era, you may have suddenly blown right past the finish line.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

And by lately, I mean the past several years or more.

The value of the S&P 500 index of stocks, where most of us hopefully have a good chunk of our retirement savings stashed into index funds, is up about fifty seven percent in just the past two years. And it has more than doubled in the past five.

In a recent development, this means that on a net worth basis, if you felt like you were only halfway to retirement as recently as the Covid Era, you may have suddenly blown right past the finish line. And some of us who were already retired long before that, may find ourselves eyeing up expensive properties or engaging in other money-burning-a-hole-in-our-pocket behaviors.

Is this real? Or is it all a bubble or some other sort of financial illusion?

As one reader recently asked me in an email:.

In a recent development, “The market seems to be in a huge bubble right now due to all sorts of hype around Artificial Intelligence. Does this make it more vulnerable to a huge crash in the future, and will it affect my retirement?”.

To answer this question, let’s take a closer look at our current somewhat unprecedented financial world and stock market. And to understand that properly, it helps to go back to the roots of what a stock is:.

A stock is a magical business arrangement which is really just a much more convenient version of a rental house.

When you own a rental house, you are entitled to collect rent. After you cover all the expenses related to the house, you get to keep the rest, and this amount is your profit.

If the average sale price of rental houses in your area goes up but the tenant keeps paying you the same amount forever, it may look good on paper but it doesn’t really mean anything unless you sell the house. And then you’d just have to turn around and pay that same higher amount for a different rental house.

Your paycheck remains unchanged unless you can make your little house rental business more profitable. So you might squeeze in a basement apartment, do some renovations, streamline expenses, or do other things to increase your net earnings.

When you eventually sell that house to another investor, the price they are willing to pay should be based on that future stream of income.

For example, if the house brings in $2000 per month ($24,000 each year) and the sale price is $240,000, the next investor is buying a business with a price-to-earnings ratio of 10, because 240k/24k=10.

It has been revealed that but if you manage to convince someone to hand over $480,000 for that same house, you’ve sold at a P/E of 20. This is a much better deal for you as the seller, but quite obviously a less rosy future for the investor buying it.

Now back to the stock market. If you put $100,000 in the market in 2019 and reinvested the dividends, today you’d already have an astonishing $256,960 (a 157% gain on your original investment).

But in that same time period, your share of tech giant earnings from that $100,000 basket of stocks has only gone from $5290 to $7540 (a measly 42% gain) – information you can get from handy analysis sites like multpl.com.

In other words, the Price-to-earnings ratio has risen from about 20 back then, to about 30 today.

Recent findings suggest that so as stock investors here in 2025, we’re just like rental house investors finding that house prices have more than doubled while rents are only up by a bit. Which makes the landlord business a lot less profitable, and we should expect exactly the same thing as stock investor: lower future profits as a percentage of our portfolio value.

Sources indicate that that doesn’t mean it’s unprofitable to own either one of these things – stocks or rental houses. But it does mean that we should expect our future income from buying them at today’s higher price-to-earnings ratio should be lower than if we could get them on sale. It’s just basic math.

But Wait! What if the Earnings are Rising?

It has been revealed that let’s say you’re considering a rental house which is a bit overpriced based on today’s rent, but you happen to know that a big Apple campus is about to get built right nearby. At that point, you expect that rent will start climbing rapidly for many years to come. In this situation, you should be willing to pay more for those future earnings when you buy the house.

This is exactly why the price of an individual company’s stock will tend to rise when some good news comes out about the company. During the Covid era, people started buying more Peloton bikes so they could exercise at home, and investors (foolishly) believed this would be a permanent trend. So Peloton stock went way up. Later, reality sunk in that this was just a fad and Peloton sales returned back to normal levels, and so did the stock.

Industry observers note that but what does it mean when the entire market goes up to much higher levels? Does it mean our entire economy is expected to grow much more promptly?

In the case of the current stock market euphoria, not exactly. Because if you dig into the share prices of the 500 massive companies that make up our famous S&P 500 index, it turns out that almost all the recent growth – about three quarters of it – came from just the seven biggest companies, known as the Magnificent Seven: Apple, Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Facebook, and sometimes Tesla.

These are all high-flying, super profitable tech companies who have seen a lot of growth and hype recently, which has caused investors to get excited and bid up their share prices in hopes of even more future growth. Collectively, they make up over 25% of the entire market value ($17.66 trillion!) and have much more expensive P/E ratios than the rest of the market (a weighted average of about 45).

If you exclude these seven biggest companies and just consider the remaining 493, you will find a P/E of only 20, which is more reasonable although still much higher than average.

What this tells us is that while investors expect the overall US economy to be fairly healthy in the coming years, they expect the biggest tech companies to continue to enjoy much faster growth.

What Does This Have To Do With Artificial Intelligence?

There’s one common theme in the big tech company boom right now: recent advances in AI have surprised the business world as software is suddenly able to display human-like reasoning in a rapidly growing number of fields. And because of this, the entire business world is fired up into a frenzy.

Six of those Magnificent Seven companies are spending hundreds of billions of dollars to build preposterously large warehouses full of supercomputers, and the lucky seventh (NVidia) is on the receiving end of those billions since they make the supercomputers and the incredible demand allows them to charge insane prices while still shipping them out by the trainload.

But that’s just the first level of this boom, the AI Infrastructure. As you move down the chain, every other industry hopes we have entered a new era of productivity and thus profits will grow faster than ever.

According to recent reports, they may actually be right: You can now do things like feed in an entire novel or legal document or piece of code and ask the AI to answer detailed questions about the characters, or identify loopholes in the contract, or even find and fix bugs for you. AI can also drive cars, identify melanoma from photographs of your skin, design medications thousands of times better than what we’re used to, and even bring humanoid robot bodies to life as mechanical workers.

The idea is that we’re on the verge of having an infinite workforce of highly intelligent AI employees who will work for us for free, eliminating the biggest constraint that humanity has had in the past: a finite supply of both intelligence and labor.

Having followed the field in some detail for a while, I personally think all this will come true, although the timeline is uncertain. And the people bidding the share prices up to these levels obviously believe it too.

But the question is, will the profits of these companies really come through at the levels they forecast? Or will there be surprises down the road: cost overruns, competition, or unexpected disasters as these newly smarter-than-us computers decide that they no longer want to be bossed around?

And what if we end up with massive unemployment and resulting social upheaval if this amazing technology puts us all out of work, leaving only Sam Altman atop his personal mountain of $100 trillion dollars taunting the world forevermore with an annoyingly quiet monotone cackle?

There’s Only One Real Answer: Nobody Really Knows!

Industry observers note that while the future is unknown, it can still be useful to use the past as a guide. After all, if you look at the history of US economic growth over time, it averages out to a surprisingly steady figure, decade after decade: about 3% after inflation.

One thing I noticed when making this graph: recent decades have actually seen slower than average growth, which is even less reason for the stock market to be priced the way it is.

Sources indicate that so What Does it all Mean? Should We Do Anything About It?

Recent findings suggest that as I said earlier, it’s still going to be profitable to own stocks for the long run, just a bit less profitable than those times when we got to buy our stocks on sale. Of course, there will be occasional manias and panics and crashes. But as always, it will be a losing game to try to time them – for example by selling all your stocks now and hoping to buy them at a cheaper price at some point in the future.

And over the long run, even if stocks return to more typical valuations, the end result would be something like the yellow line in this graph:.

Our economy will continue to grow and company earnings will grow along with it, but future investors might choose to pay a lower multiple for those earnings.

Just like when you eventually sell that rental house, you shouldn’t expect someone to pay you a million dollars for a place that only brings in $3000 of rent.

Final Thoughts And Alternative Strategies.

Sources indicate that everything we’ve covered so far is talking about the entire US stock market as a whole. And that’s what I usually focus on most because I still think this country is a uniquely good place to run a business. But what about other investing options? It’s always fun to at least look around and understand the larger investing world.

In a recent development, for starters, there’s Vanguard itself, the bedrock of the index fund world. Every year they gaze out at the investing horizon and make a ten-year forecast (guess) at future returns. This year they came up with these numbers:.

Vanguard’s updated 10-year annualized return projections:.

Wow look at that. Vanguard is forecasting that International stocks of all kinds and even bonds will outperform US stocks in the coming decade.

On the surface, this makes sense because the P/E ratio of the international stocks (for example the VXUS fund) is only 15.9, meaning those European stocks are on sale at almost 50% off compared to ours!

Just one note of caution however: Vanguard has been making this same prediction for several years and just been wrong so far. Part of the reason is that most of the AI boom seems to be happening in the US.

Longtime readers know that I’ve had a growing portion of my investments in a Betterment (robo-advisor) account over the past eleven years (see the ongoing report here). I decided to try this for precisely the reasoning above: by allocating money across more categories than just US stocks and automatically rebalancing, we should be able to see slightly higher returns with slightly lower volatility, and some tax advantages as well.

According to recent reports, so far, my experiment has drawn some heat because in retrospect, a US-only portfolio has outperformed any other option over this time period. The Betterment portfolio comes close, but the exposure to bonds and businesses in other countries has held it back, just as you’d expect. But if you believe that things will eventually balance out again in the coming decades as the Vanguard analysis suggests above, it still has a chance to catch up.

Looking at my investments there, you can review the betterment core portfolio and calculate that the weighted average of all those holdings gives us a P/E ratio of about 22.

It has been revealed that it’s always worth checking in with The Oracle on matters of the economy while we’ve still got this wonderful old sage around (see this year’s Berkshire Hathaway Shareholder letter if you want some further deep reading). And Warren is signaling that things are overvalued and bargains are few and far between. So Berkshire is holding $334 billion of uninvested cash for now, not even repurchasing its own shares which it considers slightly overvalued at the current P/E ratio which averages out to about 21 in recent years.

What About Paying Off Your House?

According to recent reports, over the long run, you usually do better if you keep a mortgage on your house and pay it off slowly, while directing all the surplus cash into index funds. But there is some point at which the opposing factors of lower expected stock returns and higher interest rates meet in the middle and this situation flips.

If you have a 7% mortgage right now, it might be a fairly close tradeoff at this point. But the real factor is how you feel about paying off your house. I happen to love being mortgage-free so I paid off my last mortgage over ten years ago and have never looked back.

Industry observers note that another way to think of this is that paying off your house is like buying a 7% bond. Definitely one of the best guaranteed returns around, and much more sensible than leaving tens of thousands of dollars in a checking or savings account unless you have a clear use for that cash.

If you’ve read any of my stock investing articles before, you’ll know that we always end up at the same place: Just relax, enjoy your life, keep investing, ignore the daily news headlines* and don’t worry.

Then reinvest that time that everyone else spends worrying into enjoying more time engaged in hard physical stuff in the great outdoors. That’s the only place where you’ll get guaranteed market-beating returns, every time.

In the Comments: what are your thoughts on the current stock market boom, future crashes and busts, and the role of Artificial Intelligence in our future?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that to stay marketable, read 10 to 20 current job postings for your role and the one a step above it, and list the skills, software, and certifications that keep showing up. Close the gap that appears most often, with your employer paying if it will, and add the newly introduced skill to your resume and LinkedIn profile.

Sources indicate that skills go stale faster than most people notice. The World Economic Forum surveyed more than 1,000 large employers worldwide for its latest Future of Jobs Report, which projects that, on average, 39% of workers’ existing skills will change or go out of date by 2030.

Recent findings suggest that you don’t have to guess which skills your field will want next. Employers spell out what they’ll pay for in every job posting, and the postings are free to read.

It has been revealed that one posting is a wish list, but a skill that turns up in most of 15 postings is a requirement. The postings for the job a step above yours show what it takes to get promoted.

According to recent reports, search your job title on Indeed or LinkedIn, then the title one step up, and open 10 to 20 current postings. Write down every skill, software program, and certification they ask for, and add a tally mark each time one repeats. The most-tallied item you don’t have yet is the gap to close first.

Sources indicate that if your applications keep stalling after graduation, run the same count on entry-level postings. A requirement that keeps showing up in postings but not on your resume could be what’s holding your applications back.

Industry observers note that close the gap the cheapest way that works. Ask your manager whether your employer’s training budget will cover a course, or take a low-cost online course on your own. You can also volunteer for a stretch assignment, a project just beyond your current role that puts the skill to use. Say a bookkeeper finds a payroll certification in most postings one step up, and one accounting software package in nearly as many. She starts with the certification and asks her manager to pay for the course, since it helps with the payroll work her team already does.

Then make the fresh skill visible to the people who decide whether you get hired or promoted. List it on your resume in the postings’ own words, add it to your LinkedIn profile, and bring one result from using it to your next performance review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, borrow audiobooks free through your library’s apps before you pay for a strategy, and place holds early on the books you want next. For a book with a wait you won’t sit through, pay for the cheapest plan that fits how you listen, and pause or cancel that plan in months you don’t need it.

Audible’s Premium proposal costs $14.95 a month, or $179.40 a year, for one credit a month, each good for an audiobook you keep. If your library offers them, Libby and Hoopla lend audiobooks free to anyone with its card.

In a recent development, hoopla’s Instant titles, marked with a lightning bolt, are always available with no wait list. A Libby title can have one, so place a hold as soon as you hear about a book you want. Suspend any hold you aren’t ready for, and you keep moving up the list without the book arriving until you unsuspend it.

Check what else your library card covers before you renew any other subscription.

Sources indicate that on a credit strategy, buy extra titles in member-only sales, and pause it in months you won’t listen. Audible lets you pause a monthly plan once every 12 months for up to 90 days, while Libro.fm lets you put your membership on hold anytime and keep your unused credits. A commuter who borrows most books but wants three fresh releases a year with long hold lists can keep a Libro.fm membership on hold except in the three months those books come out. At $14.99 a month, that’s $44.97 a year for three credits instead of $179.88 for 12.

Before you spend a credit, search Hoopla for the book, since an Instant copy there takes one of your free monthly borrows instead.

Stocks Have Fallen About 30% Around Recessions – but Usually Bottomed Before They Ended

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (452 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The S&P 500’s largest drop around a recession has averaged about 30% since 1948, but the index has usually hit bottom before the recession ended.
  • In a recent development, selling when a recession is declared often means selling after the worst is over.
  • That 30% average is our count across the 12 recessions since 1948, from Yardeni Research’s record of S&P 500 declines and the NBER’s recession dates.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The S&P 500’s largest drop around a recession has averaged about 30% since 1948, but the index has usually hit bottom before the recession ended. So don’t sell because one is coming or has just been declared. Keep money you’ll need within five years out of stocks beforehand, and keep investing on schedule through the downturn.

In a recent development, selling when a recession is declared often means selling after the worst is over. The National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), which dates U.S. recessions, declared three of the last six recessions only after the S&P 500 had hit bottom.

That 30% average is our count across the 12 recessions since 1948, from Yardeni Research’s record of S&P 500 declines and the NBER’s recession dates. In four of them, the drop stayed under 20%. The worst, 57% from October 2007 to March 2009, came with a financial crisis. Economists Carmen Reinhart and Kenneth Rogoff found that severe financial crises bring deep, long slumps in stock prices, output, and employment.

The S&P 500 usually peaked before a recession began. It hit bottom before the recession ended in 11 of the 12, most often three to six months before. The exception was 2001, when stocks didn’t hit bottom until October 2002, almost a year after that recession ended. In 2009, the low came on March 9, three months before the recession ended in June. An investor who sold and waited for the recession to end would usually have bought back after stocks had already started to rise.

It has been revealed that so prepare before a recession starts. Move money you’ll need within five years out of stocks and into a high-yield savings account, so a 30% drop can’t force you to sell low when you need the cash.

Once a recession starts, keep investing on schedule, and leave your 401(k) contributions and any automatic investments running even after it’s declared. The S&P 500 rose in the year after 11 of the 12 recessions ended, dividends included, by First Trust’s count.

At the bottom of a 30% drop, each $500 you invest buys about 43% more shares of an S&P 500 index fund than it did at the peak.

  • USDA’s latest estimates, for fiscal 2022, show nearly half of eligible people in households above the poverty line going without SNAP.
  • It has been revealed that to qualify, your household’s gross monthly income, meaning pay and other income before taxes, must stay under 130% of the federal poverty line for its size.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if your income has dropped or your pay no longer lasts the month, check whether you qualify for SNAP, the grocery benefit once called food stamps, before deciding you earn too much. Apply through your state’s SNAP office right away, since approved benefits count back to the day you apply.

USDA’s latest estimates, for fiscal 2022, show nearly half of eligible people in households above the poverty line going without SNAP.

It has been revealed that to qualify, your household’s gross monthly income, meaning pay and other income before taxes, must stay under 130% of the federal poverty line for its size. USDA’s limit for a household of four in the lower 48 states or D.C. is $3,575. USDA’s chart of state rules shows 27 states and D.C. raising that limit to 200% of the poverty line and most states dropping the federal $3,000 cap on savings. A household with someone 60 or older or disabled skips the gross income test, and its federal savings cap is $4,750.

According to recent reports, in the lower 48 states or D.C., a family of four with $2,800 a month in pay and no other income would get about $420 a month, more with high rent or child care costs and less as pay rises. The maximum there for a family of four is $1,023.

Apply through your state’s SNAP office, online where it’s offered or at a local office, and expect an interview. Bring pay stubs and your rent and utility bills as proof. The office has 30 days to decide, but a household with under $150 in monthly gross income and under $100 in cash and bank accounts can get benefits within 7 days.

According to recent reports, pregnant women, newly introduced mothers, and children under 5 can also qualify for food benefits from WIC. For rent and utilities, look into emergency help with those bills.

Adults 18 to 64 with no child under 14 at home must work, train, or volunteer 80 hours a month to keep SNAP past three months in three years, unless they’re pregnant, unable to work, or otherwise exempt. Since 2025, that rule also covers veterans and homeless adults. Report income changes as your state directs, since you must repay any overpayment.

Sources indicate that turn in the application right away with your name, address, phone number, and signature. The office accepts it that day, and a SNAP worker helps you finish the rest at the interview.

Having more than one type of debt is common, and that’s especially true once you graduate from college and start your first “real job.” You may have credit card debt, an auto loan, and a mortgage payment to make once you buy your first home. It’s also common to have other random debts to cover, including student loans.

Industry observers note that if you’re like many who took out loans during college, you will likely be paying them off after you graduate. In fact, 82% of students who borrowed loans expect to be making payments post-graduation, according to a recent College Ave Student Loans survey.

That stated, you’ll want to make sure you’re balancing debt repayment with your savings goals along the way.

You’ll also want to make sure you’re paying down debts in the optimal order, or in a way that will help you save the most money on interest as possible while aligning with your goals. Which debts should you pay off first? Here’s a rundown of how to get the best results:.

Sources indicate that no matter which types of debt you have, credit card debt should be your first priority. Why? Because credit card debt is likely the most expensive debt you have by far.

Federal Reserve data reveals the average credit card interest rate on accounts assessed interest came in at around 22% as of May 2023, yet your credit card could easily be charging higher rates than the average.

Industry observers note that to save as much money as possible, you should strive to pay as much as you can toward high-interest credit card bills each month. You can also pay down credit card debt faster with the help of a debt consolidation loan or a 0% APR balance transfer credit card.

Industry observers note that other unsecured debts like personal loan debt should come next in the debt payoff pecking order. After all, unsecured debts tend to have higher interest rates than secured debts like auto loans. In fact, the Federal Reserve also reported that the average interest rate on a 24-month personal loan came in at 11.48% as of May 2023, compared to the average rate of 7.81% on a 60-month auto loan.

Ideally, you’ll start paying more toward personal loan debt and other unsecured debts after all credit card debt is entirely paid off, although you should make at least the minimum payment on all your bills throughout the entire process.

The next debt you’ll want to tackle is your student loans. I suggest focusing on these loans after other unsecured debts, since federal student loans (and many private student loans) come with low fixed interest rates and monthly payments that will not change over time. If you have federal student loans, you may even want to look into income-driven repayment plans.

If you’re hoping to pay down student loans faster or just want to save money on interest, you can also consider refinancing your student loans to get a shorter repayment timeline, a lower monthly payment, or both. Just remember that refinancing federal student loans can mean losing access to income-driven repayment plans and federal protections like deferment and forbearance.

According to recent reports, once you have paid off or substantially paid down all your other debts, you can focus your efforts on secured debts you have like mortgage loans and auto loans. These debts should be dealt with last since they are secured with collateral and tend to offer lower interest rates as a result. For example, you can consider paying more than the minimum on your mortgage, a car loan, or both until they’re paid off completely.

Then again, you may want to pay off debts with extremely low interest rates as slowly as possible to free up more cash flow for living expenses and investments. If you took out a mortgage in January of 2021 when the average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed rate home loan was as low as 2.65%, for example, it makes sense to make the minimum payment on that debt and invest your extra cash instead.

It’s key to make sure you balance debt repayment with other financial considerations. After all, focusing too much on debt repayment early in life can leave you behind when it comes to investing for retirement or saving up for a first home.

While you’ll want to eliminate credit card debt and other high-interest debts as quickly as you can, even if you have to stop saving and investing for a while, you can pay down student loan debt and secured debts at a slower pace while saving and investing for the future along the way.

In a recent development, finally, make sure you have adequate emergency savings throughout your entire debt payoff journey, or that you begin saving for emergencies as soon as you can. Without a fully funded emergency fund, you can end up relying on credit cards and other loans to get by and ruin your debt payoff progress in the process.

Industry observers note that how much should you save? While most experts recommend having an emergency fund that can cover three to six months of expenses, it’s okay to start small if you have to.

Industry observers note that having more than one type of debt is how it works for most people, especially when you’re young and in the early stages of your career. When it comes to paying it off, however, you’ll want to make sure you have a concrete proposal that can help you reduce interest charges and get where you want to be.

Sources indicate that focusing on credit card debt and other unsecured debts first always makes sense, since these debts aren’t secured by an asset and tend to charge much higher interest rates. You can focus on student loans next, followed by other secured debts you have like a home loan or car loan.

According to recent reports, in the meantime, make sure you have an adequate emergency fund and invest in it for retirement. After all, debt won’t last forever if you’re serious about repayment, and saving and investing early can help you benefit from compound interest and avoid using credit cards for surprise expenses. Creating a budget to track these factors is your best bet.

If you need help creating one, or simply don’t know where to start, use this budget worksheet as your guide – you’ll reach financial freedom in no time.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leading economic indicators such as the yield curve tend to turn months or even years before a recession, and sometimes no recession follows.
  • Sources indicate that the Conference Board’s Leading Economic Index, which combines 10 such indicators, went nearly two years without a monthly gain after February 2022, and no recession began in that time.
  • Recent findings suggest that leading indicators shift before the wider economy does.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leading economic indicators such as the yield curve tend to turn months or even years before a recession, and sometimes no recession follows. When one flashes, don’t sell your stocks on it. Use the warning as a prompt to check your emergency fund, your initiative for a job loss, and your mix of stocks and bonds.

Sources indicate that the Conference Board’s Leading Economic Index, which combines 10 such indicators, went nearly two years without a monthly gain after February 2022, and no recession began in that time. A warning that can run two years and still be wrong can’t tell you when to sell.

Recent findings suggest that leading indicators shift before the wider economy does. Lagging ones, such as the unemployment rate, keep moving after the economy turns. The most quoted leading ones include:.

The yield curve’s record has the same catch. It inverted 6 to 24 months before each of the nine U.S. recessions from 1955 to 2018, the San Francisco Fed found, and a mid-1960s inversion brought a slowdown but no official recession. Measured as the gap between 10-year and 3-month Treasury rates, it inverted in October 2022 and stayed that way until December 2024, the St. Louis Fed’s data show, and no recession began in that time. Anyone who sold stocks when it inverted missed a rise of about 57% in the S&P 500 stock index by the time it flipped back, not counting dividends.

Industry observers note that so instead of selling, use the warning to check three things. Your emergency fund should cover three to six months of bare-bones bills. Your job-loss plan should list the costs you’d cut first and how soon to file for unemployment. And your mix of stocks and bonds should leave out money you’ll need within about five years, which belongs in savings.

Start with the emergency fund, since it helps whether or not a recession comes. An automatic transfer from each paycheck to savings builds it without selling anything.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Before you buy a washer, a printer, a phone, or anything you’ll use for years, add up each model’s cost over those years. Count the price, the energy or supplies it uses, repairs, and any interest, minus what it’ll sell for used. Then buy the model with the lower total, even when its price tag is higher.

Printers show how far apart the two totals can get. Take a $100 cartridge inkjet and a $240 ink-tank printer you refill from bottles, both from the same maker at full price.

Sources indicate that A $37 high-capacity black cartridge for the inkjet prints about 380 pages of text, about 10 cents a page. An $18 bottle of black ink for the ink-tank model prints about 4,500, under half a cent a page, and the bottles in its box print thousands of pages before you buy any.

So once the inkjet’s starter cartridges run out, the cartridges you buy cost more than the $140 you saved on the printer within about 1,500 pages of text. That’s two and a half years at 50 pages a month, or 12 and a half years at 10.

To compare any two models, total each one over the years you’ll keep it:.

These totals assume both models last as long as you’ll keep them, and how long each one lasts decides whether buying the cheapest option saves money. The same math works out what owning a car costs and what owning a home costs, with bigger items such as insurance and property taxes.

It has been revealed that for the number of years, use how long you kept your last one. The longer you’ll keep it, the more the running costs, rather than the price tag, decide which model is cheaper.

Remodel for Yourself – Small Projects Recoup the Most When You Sell

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Most home improvements add less to your sale price than they cost, and the bigger the project, the less of its cost you get back.
  • Value report compares the average cost of 28 common remodeling projects with what each adds to a home’s sale price.
  • Recent findings suggest that small, visible projects lead the list.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Most home improvements add less to your sale price than they cost, and the bigger the project, the less of its cost you get back. Remodel for your own use, and if you’ll sell within a few years, pick small, visible projects like a new garage door or entry door, which recoup the most.

Zonda’s 2025 Cost vs. Value report compares the average cost of 28 common remodeling projects with what each adds to a home’s sale price. By its national averages, only five added more than they cost, and each of those cost less than $30,000.

Recent findings suggest that small, visible projects lead the list. A latest garage door cost an average $4,672 and added an estimated $12,507, and a steel entry door averaged $2,435 and added $5,270. Manufactured stone veneer on the lower front of the house and fiber-cement siding also paid for themselves. So did a midrange minor kitchen remodel, which keeps the cabinet boxes but replaces the doors, counters, and appliances.

Industry observers note that massive projects sit near the bottom. A midrange primary suite addition averaged $170,517 and recouped 32% of its cost, an upscale major kitchen remodel 36%, and an upscale suite addition 18%. A buyer pays for what most buyers want, and a big remodel is built to one owner’s taste. So remodel for the years you’ll live in the house, and choose projects for resale only when a sale is near.

Planning to sell within three years? By those averages, a new garage door and steel entry door would cost about $7,100 together and add about $17,800, so you’d come out about $10,700 ahead. The midrange suite addition would add about $55,100 for its $170,517 and leave you about $115,400 behind.

Sources indicate that before any upgrade, keep the roof, furnace, plumbing, and wiring sound and up to code. A buyer’s inspection will turn up a failing one, and you’ll pay to fix it or take a lower offer. Keep a kitchen or bath in line with the houses around you, too. A midrange bath remodel recouped 80% of its $26,138 average cost, and an upscale one 42% of $81,612.

Favor energy upgrades that pay for themselves in lower bills, since solar panels recouped just 30% of their $55,937 average cost at sale.

Buyers judge a remodel by its condition, not its cost, so a kitchen redone 10 years before you list is priced as a 10-year-old kitchen.

Pick a free checking account, or one that waives its monthly fee for something you already do each month. Then make sure it has fee-free ATMs near home and work, plus an app that deposits checks.

Your employer needs the account’s routing and account numbers to set up direct deposit, and you can write paper checks to a landlord or anyone else who won’t take a card. A savings account holds money you’re keeping and pays interest on it, while checking moves money in and out, so you choose a checking account by its fees and how easy it is to use.

Two accounts with the same debit card, app, and direct deposit can cost different amounts to keep. One charges $15 any month your balance falls below $1,500, and the other charges nothing. If your balance falls below $1,500 every month, the second saves you $180 a year for the same service.

According to recent reports, start with the kind you need, whether that’s a no-frills basic account, interest checking, rewards checking, a student account, or a second-chance account. Interest and rewards checking often pay their top rate or cash back only in months you meet their rules, such as a set number of debit card purchases. A second-chance account is for people a bank turned down because of trouble with a past account, such as an unpaid overdraft.

Then check these five things before you open one.

Choose an account whose monthly fee you’d avoid even in a tight month, since falling short of the waiver once means paying the full fee that month.

According to recent reports, take an owner whose house rents for $2,000 a month and leaves him $200 a month after the mortgage and other costs. A manager charging 10% of the rent, the middle of the typical range according to the National Association of Residential Property Managers, would cost him $2,400 a year. If a fresh tenant moves in every two years, a leasing fee of half a month’s rent adds $500 a year. His $2,400 yearly profit becomes a $500 loss. On cash alone, managing it himself beats hiring by $2,900 a year, so the choice comes down to his time.

According to recent reports, say he lives 300 miles away and would spend about 100 hours a year on the house, trips and late-night calls included. The manager costs him $29 for each of those hours and spares him the cost of the trips. If an hour of his time is worth more than $29, hiring beats doing the work himself, provided he can cover the $500 yearly loss.

If your hours are worth more than the manager’s cost per hour, vet each management company before you sign.

This full-length adventure documentary follows kayaker Dane Jackson and a small team down Chile’s remote and wild Rio Cuervo.

Industry observers note that with an entire river to descend, the film wastes no time getting right into it. Dane Jackson launches into the complicated business of trip logistics, trying to find a way to get the team and their equipment to the beginning of the river. Besides him, the team consists of the trip’s mastermind, Kilian Astorga, and kayakers Tom Dolle, Eirik Hansen, Adrian Mattern, and David Sodomka.

Forty years ago, there was a road up to Lake Mayuin, the volcanic pool from with Rio Cuervo flows. It’s gone now, so they turn to helicopter transport. With their gear dangling below on a rope, the chopper carries them up into the mountain, depositing kayaks and kayakers alike on the lakeshore. They set up camp and settle in to begin the first descent of the Rio Cuervo.

It has been revealed that the team scouts the head of the river, swelled with recent rainfall. Photo: Screenshot.

Sources indicate that the dense forest and sometimes steep banks add another layer of difficulty as they begin to make their way downstream. They have to initiative ahead, as there are stretches where it is impossible to bail if the rapids become too much. This means more portaging, which is painfully slow due to the thick vegetation.

Sources indicate that when they do hit the rapids, on-board cameras capture the frenetic energy of whitewater kayaking. But the film makes no attempt to conceal the reality of a first descent. Much of their time is spent scouting ahead by drone, poring over satellite images, portaging, and standing about debating logistics.

It has been revealed that sunset arrives before the end of their portage. Camping in the jungle makes for an uncomfortable night. Photo: Screenshot.

Jackson and the rest of the crew soldier on, though, cracking nerdy jokes (the jungle is compared to both Dagobah and Fangorn Forest) and making the best of bad weather and rough camping. In the final few days, conditions improve, and they can spend more time on the water.

Industry observers note that the contrast between their slow, grueling push forward and the wild speed on the river brings refreshing energy to the kayaking sections. When the river finally widens as they glide into the sea, it feels like a hard-won victory.

In a recent development, running a 3.5km gorge. Photo: Screenshot.

Industry observers note that early in the production of a certain musical, Broadway director Harold Prince attempted to ask Andrew Lloyd Weber what the deeper political allegory or social commentary was behind the composer’s feline opus. Weber famously took a long pause and replied: “Hal, this is just about cats.”.

This movie is about kayaking. Many outdoor adventure films use the genre, and the adventure story, to explore grand themes, and some do so successfully. But when they fall flat, is it more annoying than I can begin to express. For that reason, I deeply respect the clarity of purpose evinced by Dan Jackson and First Descent Rio Cuervo.

File Jointly Unless Medical Bills or Income-Driven Loan Payments Make Separate Returns Cheaper

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (493 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if you’re married, file your taxes jointly unless separate returns save you more than they cost.
  • In a recent development, keeping separate bank accounts doesn’t call for separate tax returns.
  • Separate filers can’t claim the education credits or the student loan interest deduction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you’re married, file your taxes jointly unless separate returns save you more than they cost. Filing separately gives up several credits and deductions, but it can win when one of you has substantial medical bills or an income-driven student loan payment. Prepare your return both ways before you file.

In a recent development, keeping separate bank accounts doesn’t call for separate tax returns. File jointly by default, since the IRS indicates separate returns generally cost a couple more combined tax.

Separate filers can’t claim the education credits or the student loan interest deduction. Couples who live together also lose the earned income and child care credits. Through 2028, the newly introduced deductions for tips, overtime, and seniors require a joint return too. If one of you itemizes deductions, the other loses the standard deduction.

Spouses who lived apart for the last six months of the year should check which filing status they qualify for first. In a community property state, separate returns split your combined earnings in half.

Two situations can still make separate returns cheaper. One is substantial medical bills for the spouse with the lower income. Itemized medical costs are deductible only above 7.50% of adjusted gross income, and a separate return applies that threshold to one income instead of two. Only bills that spouse paid count, and the deduction must outweigh what separate returns give up.

The other is an income-driven student loan plan, which generally counts only the borrower’s income when you file separately. Say only you have student loans, repaid on the Repayment Assistance Plan. Your adjusted gross income is $36,000, your spouse’s is $32,000, and you have no kids. A joint return sets your payment at 6% of $68,000, or $4,080 a year, and a separate one at 3% of $36,000, or $1,080. Filing separately wins unless it adds more than $3,000 to your tax.

Sources indicate that separate returns also protect you from a spouse’s tax problems. On a joint return, either of you can owe all of its tax, interest, and penalties, even on income only one of you earned, so doubts about your spouse’s return can justify filing separately.

Settle the choice before the due date. After that, a joint return can’t be changed to separate ones, though separate returns can generally be amended into a joint return for up to three years.
