#114655. How to Navigate the Tariff Circus

📅 13 Jun 2025 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2418 w)
📖 Baca
Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mrmoneymustache ↗ Open Full Page

How to Navigate the Tariff Circus

📅 13 Jun 2025 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2418 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Quite accidentally, it looks like we timed our last talk about the stock market pretty darned well.
  • And although stock market volatility doesn’t always come with an easily labeled explanation, this time the reason seems pretty clear: it’s the Tariffs.
  • As our financial world has been whipped around like a circus tent in a hurricane for the last several months, almost everyone who has a stake in this country has been wondering what to make of it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quite accidentally, it looks like we timed our last talk about the stock market pretty darned well. Back in February 2025, the market put the perfect cap on a multi year climb before stepping onto the wild roller coaster we’re at the moment riding. Since then it has seen some of the steepest drops and recoveries in history, losing a full 20% of its value at the bottom while somehow managing to end up right back near the peak as I’m writing this.

And although stock market volatility doesn’t always come with an easily labeled explanation, this time the reason seems pretty clear: it’s the Tariffs.

As our financial world has been whipped around like a circus tent in a hurricane for the last several months, almost everyone who has a stake in this country has been wondering what to make of it.

Recent findings suggest that as I write this, we still don’t know the outcome of the worldwide tariff and trade battle that our unpredictable government has unleashed upon the world. But we’re already seeing the results: businesses are bracing for massive changes, currencies and interest rates are reacting, and regular investors like you and me are wondering what the future holds for our early retirement funds. Surveying my own group of friends, the reactions span the whole range of emotions from “this is a giant Nothingburger” to “we’re all totally screwed.”.

So what’s the real answer? To get closer to that, we should start with the most basic question of:.

A tariff is just a sales tax charged by our government on goods which are imported into the country. They are paid by whoever is doing the importing – meaning you if you order something like an e-bike directly from a manufacturer in China, or by companies like Amazon, Walmart, or Apple which import products from other countries by the shipload.

Sources indicate that but in the end, the tariffs aren’t paid by China or Amazon or Apple. They are paid by you, the end consumer, because if their cost of goods increases, a retailer is of course going to raise their prices to continue to make a profit.

Industry observers note that tariffs also affect companies directly: if Home Depot wants to build a new store or Chevron needs a new oil rig, the tariffs on imported steel, copper, lumber and a million other components will raise the cost of these construction projects. And they raise the cost of housing, because most of the building materials in houses come from multiple countries as well.

Recent findings suggest that on average, tariffs will result in higher prices for everything just like any other broad-based sales tax. And just like most other taxes, the overall effect is to slow the economy and reduce our spending power. On the positive side, all that tax money flows into the government’s pocket which could help fund the national budget and even reduce the deficit.

Of course, every government needs at least some tax revenue to function, so it makes sense to use some mix of sales, income and corporate taxes to get there. The most important part is that the levels need to be as low as possible while still keeping the country running well, and as fair and predictable as possible, so that people and businesses have an incentive to work hard and the ability to initiative far into the future.

Sources indicate that and that’s where our current tariff regime gets it completely backwards. Donald Trump is throwing around random, extremely high tariff numbers as threats, then walking them back and changing them on an almost daily basis..

Whoa, that Sounds Mostly Bad – Is There a Good Side of Tariffs?

Sometimes, a country will use tariffs to protect their own domestic industries. For example, if you put a tax on imported Hondas, then General Motors cars will gain a competitive advantage – so GM will make more money. In this example, most consumers end up losing due to increased prices and decreased selection. But at least domestic auto manufacturers and their employees are happy.

This can be strategic (for example we might want to slap a tax on imported fighter jets to make sure Boeing and Lockheed can remain in business, for national defense purposes.) Or it can be corrupt (a politician might receive funding from kingpins in the steel industry, and in return then push through tariffs on imported steel to protect the profits of US steelmakers.).

In a recent development, and this isn’t just a Trump or Republican thing either – Joe Biden used tariffs during his terms in an attempt to please swing-state voters. One of the worst examples was a tax on imported solar panel components (which Trump has since raised even further, proving that Boneheadedness can be Bipartisan). These are sheets of cheap glass that literally pump the cheapest energy and easiest wealth into your country for 30 years as soon as you plug them in. Cheap energy lowers everyone’s cost of living while also boosting industry. There is no good reason to block such wealth from flowing across your borders.

Can Tariffs Bring Us More Jobs?

Let’s go back to that hypothetical tax on Hondas, and let’s say it’s a massive one like $5000. At that level, many buyers will start heading over to the GM dealer next door to consider what he’s selling. Sure, the GM cars may not be as good, but for five grand some people are going to settle in order to save some money.

Sources indicate that because of this, GM’s sales go up. So they hire more employees and build more factories. They might even develop some new models and new technologies in response to all that new demand. More people learn advanced skills and in the best case it becomes a virtuous circle.

Sources indicate that but in exchange for this boom in the auto industry, everyone else has to pay more for slightly shittier cars and trucks. Higher vehicle prices means Amazon will have to spend more on their delivery fleet, so they will raise prices slightly on everything they sell. Somewhere a startup company or a medical breakthrough will be just a bit less likely to happen, because they are operating in an environment that is just a bit more expensive and a bit less efficient.

On top of that, with GM liberated from the hassle of competing with Honda, it will have less incentive to innovate and streamline itself. So its overall trajectory will be slower and less efficient even if its profits are higher.

According to recent reports, this major picture effect is why most economists agree that tariffs should be used very sparingly. They almost always cause unexpected damage, decrease overall employment and slow down an economy, but sometimes (like for food security or national defense) those costs are worth paying.

So Why is Donald Trump Throwing Around Tariffs Like They Are The Best Thing Ever?

This has been confusing to almost everyone. If you take him at his word, he appears to have a Bizarro Opposite Universe belief system about economics. Donald has claimed in speeches that the tariffs will somehow make us wealthier. He’s focusing on the first-order effects like GM hiring more workers, while completely ignoring the fact that everything else in the country gets less efficient in exchange.

Sources indicate that but when he unveils larger tariffs, share prices go down, because everyone who actually runs or invests in US companies knows that of course they will make less money on average. When tariffs are paused or reduced, share prices go back up. Yet he keeps wielding the threats and we go back and forth.

It seems to be obvious to everyone except Donald himself that Tariffs are just a national sales tax rather than some clever sneaky strategic weapon, which leads to various theories that okay, maybe he knows that too but is just pretending in order to gain some influence.

The basic theory goes like this:.

So right now our entire economy is subject to the whims of a single person.. And as long as this is the case, we’re just the same as any other dictatorship – something our constitution was supposed to prevent with the whole “three independent branches of government” thing.

But presidents have tried to break out of their constitutional cage and get more power many times in the past, and this is just the latest example. The real test will be if our system eventually manages to stop this abuse and put itself back in balance as it always has in the past. You can already see this fight beginning to play out in our court system, in this Economist article:.

How Big are the Tariffs Right Now?

Even without the 145% nonsense numbers that were thrown around a few months ago, they are still far higher than they have been in the last 75 years or more. While it would be hard to pin down the current numbers in a stationary blog post like this one, the key thing to remember is that our current US economy is built around very low tariffs and relatively free trade.

Why haven’t I noticed Prices Going Up Yet?

While the US economy is fueled by a constant stream of cargo ships, as a whole we function like the biggest cargo ship of all: we have a huge inventory and it takes a while to change directions.

So in normal times, we already have several months of inventory of most things in the country. And then when all this drama started, importers started placing even more orders to stockpile things in advance before the tariffs hit. And now that they are in place, we’re importing a lot less stuff.

It has been revealed that for now, we’re still using up the stockpiled inventory, but imports have dropped significantly so we’re promptly running out of cheap goods. If that happens, we will probably start seeing shortages and price increases throughout this summer or fall. For some things like plastic party trinkets, we can do just fine without. But if we lose access to core useful things like tools and machinery, the economic consequences will be much less fun.

The Dark Side and the Bright Side.

The most important phrase to remember in US politics and economics is the phrase “This too shall pass.” The only mystery right now is that we don’t know exactly how it will pass. So we could sketch out a few scenarios:.

1) The current crazy-high tariffs really do stick around:.

I personally think this is the less likely scenario because nobody really wants it. But just as a thought experiment, it might go something like this:.

2) They do end up being just a negotiating tactic and we go back to mostly low tariffs.

In other words, the best way to win the tariff game is not to play it.

Sources indicate that just as much of US prosperity is built upon our huge population of 330 million people living in 50 states with open borders and no trade restrictions, all (friendly) countries of the world can benefit from the free exchange of goods, services and even people. We’re all human beings and if we treat each other with a collaborative respect, we all grow richer.

Epilogue: Is it Almost Over Already?

I started writing this article on April 2nd, when Donald announced his “Liberation Day” and the stock market reacted with the biggest drop since 1932. Some people panicked and locked in massive losses despite decades of warnings from your favorite financial bloggers, like this unfortunate soul in the comments to a JL Collins post:.

But as I watched over the next two months, we have bounced our way back up – with each drop in proposed tariffs triggering a corresponding increase in stock prices (a measure of investor enthusiasm of how bright our future looks).

Right now, the US stock market is just about back to its all-time high. This doesn’t match with our current level of tariffs, which are still about seven times higher than they were before the circus opened. But it demonstrates that investors believe it’s all going to end with a truce and a resumption of free-ish international trade.

Industry observers note that if they’re wrong, the roller coaster ride will still have some more fun in store for us. But as long as we eventually end our current experiment in “emergency” tariff dictatorship and get back to functioning as a democracy, things should be just fine in the long run. I’m still 100% invested myself, so that’s where I place my bet.

The Biggest Lesson: Don’t Form Your Opinions Based on News Headlines.

Recent findings suggest that decades ago in a brighter age of journalism, there may have been a time when headlines were designed primarily to inform us, with just a bit of sizzle and spice to pull in our attention. Unfortunately, nowadays the priorities have flipped where the primary goal is attention, and accuracy carries little or no weight. Even a totally inaccurate article makes money for the publisher.

So while Democrats and Republicans like to do battle over which media sources are biased, in reality they’re all wrong: all click-funded commercial media is biased – sometimes politically but even more importantly biased towards generating outrage and fear, because those generate more money.

There are two solutions to this:.

1) Either ignore the media completely and focus on your own life, or.

2) Become a subject matter expert on things you really care about, and then read the original sources whenever you want to learn about something.

Sources indicate that I mostly practice option #1, but as a science and technology nerd I get into #2 in just the areas I find most interesting. And it’s amazing how the more deeply you understand a subject, the more you see just how wrong most media stories are about your area of expertise. Which means they’re probably pretty wrong about almost everything.

So as always, with this lesson learned it’s time to shut down that phone and laptop, exhale all our worries and get back outside with your real-life family and friends. See you in a few months!

Split Bills by Income When One Partner Earns Much More – Keep Fun Money Equal

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that when one of you earns far more, split shared bills in proportion to take-home pay instead of 50/50, and give each of you the same personal spending money, no questions asked.
  • According to recent reports, A 50/50 split looks fair until your incomes are far apart.
  • Having the higher earner cover everything removes that strain, but it can give that partner more say over how the household’s money gets spent.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that when one of you earns far more, split shared bills in proportion to take-home pay instead of 50/50, and give each of you the same personal spending money, no questions asked. Then protect the lower earner by deciding big purchases together and saving for retirement in both names.

According to recent reports, A 50/50 split looks fair until your incomes are far apart. If one of you takes home $7,000 a month and the other $3,000, splitting $5,000 in shared bills down the middle takes about 36% of the higher earner’s pay and 83% of the lower earner’s.

Having the higher earner cover everything removes that strain, but it can give that partner more say over how the household’s money gets spent. A split by income avoids both problems, since each of you puts the same share of your own pay toward the bills. Here that’s 70% and 30% of the $5,000, or $3,500 and $1,500, which is half of each partner’s take-home pay.

It has been revealed that on its own, the split still leaves each of you the other half of your pay, $3,500 for the higher earner against $1,500 for the lower earner. So each of you keeps the same allowance of fun money, say $300 a month, to spend without explaining it, and what’s left, $3,200 and $1,200 here, goes to savings goals you set together.

It has been revealed that to find your own split, divide each partner’s take-home pay by your combined total. Each of you then pays your share into a joint account for shared bills on payday. The same split works when one of you cuts back to care for kids. The bigger paycheck covers most or all of the bills, and the equal allowance means the partner who cut back never has to ask for spending money.

Then protect the partner who earns less. Make any purchase over an agreed amount, say $500, a joint decision, even when the higher earner pays for it. Keep retirement saving going in both names. If you’re married and file jointly, a spousal IRA lets one paycheck fund an individual retirement account for each of you. And buy term life insurance on the higher earner’s life, since losing that income would cut your household’s take-home pay by 70% here.

Rerun the percentages the month either take-home pay changes, whether from a raise, a new job, or a move to part-time hours.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treat lottery tickets as entertainment you pay for, never as a blueprint to get ahead.
  • In a recent development, A record jackpot can make a few extra tickets feel like a smart move.
  • In a recent development, those odds are 1 in 292.2 million for a $2 Powerball play and 1 in 290.5 million for a $5 Mega Millions play.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treat lottery tickets as entertainment you pay for, never as a blueprint to get ahead. On average, states pay out about 67 cents in prizes for every dollar of tickets sold, and the Powerball jackpot is a 1-in-292-million shot. Set a monthly limit near what a night out costs you, and stop once it’s spent.

In a recent development, A record jackpot can make a few extra tickets feel like a smart move. Each ticket’s odds stay the same, though, however big the prize grows.

In a recent development, those odds are 1 in 292.2 million for a $2 Powerball play and 1 in 290.5 million for a $5 Mega Millions play. Across all lottery games, states sold $104.7 billion in tickets in fiscal 2024 and paid out $70.2 billion in prizes, the Census Bureau reports. Players as a group lost about a third of what they spent. That loss is a fair price for a few days of daydreaming, but it rules tickets out as a way to build wealth.

Industry observers note that in a national survey for a National Bureau of Economic Research study, lottery spending fell only modestly as income rose. That means lower-income households spend a bigger share of what they earn on tickets than higher earners do. Pay for your tickets only with money left after bills and savings.

A $20-a-week habit costs $1,040 a year. Invest that $1,040 at the end of each year for 20 years instead, at an assumed 7% annual return, and you’d have about $42,600, more than double the $20,800 you put in. Keep the ticket budget small, and save or invest what you’d have spent beyond it.

If you enjoy playing, these steps keep the thrill and limit what it costs.

Count every ticket as money spent the moment you buy it, since about 24 of every 25 Powerball plays win nothing at all.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that run a rental’s numbers yourself before you offer: what it nets each month after every expense and the mortgage, what you earn on the cash you put in, and how well its income covers the loan.
  • A rental can pass the 1% rule and still leave you almost nothing each month.
  • It has been revealed that say a $210,000 house rents for $2,100, exactly 1% of its price.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that run a rental’s numbers yourself before you offer: what it nets each month after every expense and the mortgage, what you earn on the cash you put in, and how well its income covers the loan. The 1% rule, monthly rent at 1% of the price, only tells you which listings deserve that math.

A rental can pass the 1% rule and still leave you almost nothing each month. A listing’s projected return uses someone else’s assumptions, not yours.

It has been revealed that say a $210,000 house rents for $2,100, exactly 1% of its price. Taxes, insurance, repairs, savings for major replacements like a roof, and rent lost to empty months come to $9,600 a year. You put down 20%, or $42,000, pay $6,000 in closing costs, and borrow the other $168,000 on a 30-year investment-property loan at 8%.

A year’s rent minus every cost but the mortgage is the net operating income, here $15,600. Divide it by the price for the cap rate, 7.4%. The $1,233 monthly loan payment leaves $67 a month of cash flow, or $807 a year, which is a 1.7% cash-on-cash return on the $48,000 you put in. Many lenders check a version of the debt service coverage ratio, net operating income divided by a year of loan payments, and here it’s 1.05, barely above the 1.0 at which the income just covers the loan. Pay a property manager 8% of the rent, and you lose $101 a month.

Before you offer, swap each of the listing’s assumptions for your own:.

In a recent development, compare your total with the 50% rule, which puts every cost but the mortgage at about half the rent. A total far below half the rent is a sign you missed a cost.

In a recent development, last, rerun the cash flow with an extra month empty, with rent 10% lower, and with a fresh roof in year one. Offer no more than the price at which the cash flow stays above zero in the first two cases, and keep enough cash on hand to replace the roof.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pour laundry detergent to the fill line your label gives for your load size, not to the brim of the cap, and the same jug lasts for more loads. In the bathroom, use a small dab of shampoo, a pea-size bit of toothpaste, and a foaming pump filled with soap thinned with water.

Every extra splash of detergent or squeeze of shampoo is product you paid for and then rinsed down the drain.

In a recent development, the dose on a detergent label is set for typical wash conditions and gives the best cleaning, says the American Cleaning Institute, the trade group for cleaning-product makers. Pour past it for an ordinary load and the jug just empties sooner. Too much detergent can even leave residue on your clothes, Whirlpool says.

Say your jug’s label promises 64 loads at the medium-load line, and you’ve been pouring 50% more than that each time. The jug runs out after about 43 loads. Pour to the line and you get all 64 loads instead of 43, about 50% more, so two jugs now do the work of three.

Start with the fill line for your load size, using a high-efficiency (HE) detergent if your washer is an HE model. Then use less for a small or lightly soiled load or soft water, and more for a large or heavily soiled load or hard water (water high in minerals), as the institute advises.

The same goes for the bathroom shelf.

Before your next load, find the fill line your detergent’s label gives for the load you wash most, and pour to it every time.

Buy a Rental for Its Cash Flow – Treat Price Gains as a Bonus

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (480 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, A rental that loses money each month is a bet that home prices will rise, and when they stall or fall, you keep covering the shortfall or sell at a loss.
  • Recent findings suggest that picture an investor who bought a condo in 2006 expecting price gains of 10% a year to make up for rent that fell $1,000 a month short of its costs.
  • A rental with negative cash flow, meaning rent that falls short of its costs, pays off only if prices climb fast enough to cover the shortfall.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, A rental that loses money each month is a bet that home prices will rise, and when they stall or fall, you keep covering the shortfall or sell at a loss. Buy one whose rent covers every cost, from the mortgage to repairs and vacancies, and treat any rise in value as extra.

Recent findings suggest that picture an investor who bought a condo in 2006 expecting price gains of 10% a year to make up for rent that fell $1,000 a month short of its costs. By 2011 the condo was worth 30% less, and the investor sold at a loss after paying $60,000 to cover five years of shortfalls.

A rental with negative cash flow, meaning rent that falls short of its costs, pays off only if prices climb fast enough to cover the shortfall. Every repair and every vacancy adds to the shortfall, and borrowing makes a price drop worse. With 20% down, a 20% fall in price wipes out your whole down payment, because the loan doesn’t shrink when the price does.

The Federal Housing Finance Agency’s national index of home prices fell nearly 20% from its April 2007 peak by March 2011. In Austin, Texas, home prices jumped nearly 60% from 2020 to 2022, then the median price fell 22% from its pandemic peak by mid-2025, the Texas Real Estate Research Center found. Over the long run, most of what houses earned came from rent. In a typical year from 1890 to 2006, a house returned about 9% after inflation, with 7.7% from rent, before expenses, and only 1.3% from rising prices, a Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia working paper found.

In a recent development, so buy only a property whose rent covers the mortgage, taxes, insurance, and a budget for repairs and vacancies. In an expensive market, that may mean buying in a city where rent still covers a mortgage. Run the full numbers before you make an offer. If the rent falls short, put more down to shrink the payment, or wait for a property that pays its own way.

Count the loan balance you pay down each month, and any rise in value, as your long-run gain, not as money toward the monthly costs.

You can hold a rental that covers its own costs through a slump, because the rent, not your paycheck, keeps paying the loan.

#114646. Skip Fabric Softener & Dryer Sheets – Most Loads Don’t Need Them

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (466 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Moneycrashers ↗ Open Full Page

Skip Fabric Softener & Dryer Sheets – Most Loads Don’t Need Them

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (466 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Stop buying fabric softener and dryer sheets by habit.
  • It has been revealed that A $13 jug of Downy covers 190 medium loads, and a $10 box of Bounce holds 240 sheets.
  • Both work by coating fibers so they feel smoother and cling less, and that coating is the catch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stop buying fabric softener and dryer sheets by habit. Softener can make towels less absorbent and leave a residue that traps odor in workout clothes, and most other laundry comes out fine without either. For static, dry your synthetic fabrics in their own load and take them out as soon as they’re dry.

It has been revealed that A $13 jug of Downy covers 190 medium loads, and a $10 box of Bounce holds 240 sheets. A family that washes the roughly 300 loads a year ENERGY STAR says is average, using a medium dose and one sheet each time, spends about 11 cents a load, or about $33 a year.

Both work by coating fibers so they feel smoother and cling less, and that coating is the catch. Consumer Reports says liquid softener leaves a film that makes towels less absorbent and more flammable. Nike says softener leaves a residue on workout clothes that traps odor-causing bacteria and that sheets clog the fabric, so detergent has a harder time getting in. CHOICE, Australia’s consumer group, warns that softeners can also weaken the flame resistance of children’s sleepwear.

So check the care label before reaching for softener, and keep it away from towels, workout clothes, kids’ pajamas, and anything labeled flame resistant. Softener changes how fabric feels, not how clean it gets, so the rest of the wash can skip it too.

For static, the fix costs nothing. Whirlpool, the appliance maker, says synthetics such as polyester and nylon are especially prone to static and that over-drying makes it worse. So dry them in a load of their own on low heat or the dryer’s moisture-sensing setting.

Wool dryer balls, sold as a reusable swap for sheets, start at about $9 for a set of six, roughly a quarter of the $33 a year that softener and sheets cost. Whirlpool says wool balls help prevent static by absorbing moisture. But a 2016 test by Consumer NZ found no less static and no softer clothes with dryer balls. CHOICE’s 2024 test found that none of the balls it tried did much for drying time or energy use. Treat them as optional.

Use up the jug and box you have, then leave both off the shopping list and keep about $33 a year.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Colorado couple Jules Stennes and Patch Doyle have cycled 6,124km along the newly opened Golden Gravel Trail.
  • The trail crosses eight states — Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, and Oregon — and stretches from Cape Girardeau on the banks of the Mississippi River to the small town of Port Orford on the edge of the Pacific Ocean.
  • Most of the route, roughly 70%, is unpaved.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Colorado couple Jules Stennes and Patch Doyle have cycled 6,124km along the newly opened Golden Gravel Trail. The Adventure Cycling Association created the route this year to celebrate its 50th anniversary.

The trail crosses eight states — Missouri, Kansas, Oklahoma, Colorado, Utah, Wyoming, Idaho, and Oregon — and stretches from Cape Girardeau on the banks of the Mississippi River to the small town of Port Orford on the edge of the Pacific Ocean.

Most of the route, roughly 70%, is unpaved. It is the organization’s longest off-road cycling trail, 1,120km longer than the Great Divide Mountain Bike Route.

The Golden Gravel Trail route. Photo: The Adventure Cycling Association.

In a recent development, stennes and Doyle finished in Cape Girardeau after 73 days, averaging an impressive 80km and around 12 hours of pedaling per day. “About 90% of it is mental,” they told Heartland News. “You might be tired, but you just keep on moving.”.

The couple are both experienced long-distance cyclists who have previously finished Montana’s Big Sky Spectaculaire in six days and nine hours in 2022 (a self-supported 1,400km ultra-endurance race), among other bikepacking trips.

Jules Stennes and Patch Doyle during the 2022 Significant Sky Spectaculaire. Photo: Bikepacking.com.

Likewise, the Adventure Cycling Association suggests riders should be self-supported for the Golden Gravel Trail. Riders are advised to carry two or three days’ worth of food for the route’s most isolated sections, and up to a day’s worth of water. This is particularly important in the more arid sections, such as eastern Oregon. In Colorado, Utah, and Idaho, the trail traverses subranges of the Rockies and crosses the route’s highest point, Cumberland Pass at 3,668 m, in Colorado.

Stennes and Doyle say their journey included thunderstorms, aggressive farm dogs, and “countless hills.”.

Screen Tenants by a Standard You Wrote Before Listing – Not by First Impressions

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (407 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that before you list a rental, write down the income, credit, landlord references, and eviction history an applicant needs.
  • Turning away the wrong applicant costs a little more time with the unit empty.
  • A standard set before you meet anyone keeps a good first impression from outweighing a bad rental history.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that before you list a rental, write down the income, credit, landlord references, and eviction history an applicant needs. Then verify each one for every applicant instead of taking the application’s word for it. One written standard helps you pick tenants who pay and keeps your decisions within fair housing law.

Turning away the wrong applicant costs a little more time with the unit empty. Removing the wrong tenant can take a court case and months of lost rent.

A standard set before you meet anyone keeps a good first impression from outweighing a bad rental history. Say an applicant charms you at the showing, but their last landlord reports two months of unpaid rent. A standard that asks for on-time rent at the last two rentals rules them out, and the unit goes to the next complete application.

The Fair Housing Act bars most landlords from turning anyone away because of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or having children under 18. A standard applied the same way to everyone is your record of why you turned someone down. In many states and cities, source-of-income laws also bar refusing an applicant whose housing voucher pays part of the rent.

A workable standard covers four things.

It has been revealed that if you check criminal records, write down which convictions count and how far back you’ll look, within your state’s and city’s rules. Upcoming Jersey and New York City make most landlords wait to run a criminal check until they’ve offered the unit, pending its result, to an applicant who meets the rest of the standard.

Use one written application for everyone, and keep its fee within what your state allows.

Hand every applicant the standard in writing before you take a fee or run a check. Washington requires landlords to share their criteria, in writing or posted, before any screening, and elsewhere it spares an applicant who can’t qualify a wasted fee.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Search teams have found the body of Wolfgang Waschiczek, 57, of Germany, who went missing after he reached Camp 3 on his way down from the summit. Evidence demonstrates he fell 1,700m to his death.

Waschiczek was one among over 200 climbers who lined up toward the summit of Ama Dablam this past weekend. He reached the top on October 25 with guide Sonam Sherpa, but for some reason the two of them stopped descending at a rather high point on the mountain.

“The pair decided to stay at Camp 3 overnight after borrowing a sleeping bag and other gear from other climbers,” his expedition outfitter, Real Himalaya Nepal, told The Tourism Times.

Climbers above Camp 3 on Ama Dablam. Photo: Dorjee Gyalzen Sherpa.

Sources indicate that according to the outfitter, the climbers prepared to continue down this morning. Lama asked his client to stay in place while he returned the sleeping bag to the tent where he had borrowed it. When the Sherpa returned, Waschiczek was nowhere to be found, but his crampons were still there, which suggested a freak fall. A search helicopter was called, and the remains of the climber were found this afternoon at around 4,500m.

Waschiczek is the first fatality on Ama Dablam this season.

Together with Manaslu, Ama Dablam is the most popular fall mountain in Nepal. The latest enhancement from Nepal’s Department of Tourism on October 17 highlighted that over 300 foreign climbers had applied for a climbing permit. That day, the rope-fixing team opened the route to the top, and a massive summit wave started a couple of days later.

Industry observers note that virtually all foreign climbers are guided by one or two Sherpas, so the summit rates and numbers are remarkable. Local media estimate that over 200 climbers, among locals and foreigners, have topped out so far this season. Further teams should join them over the rest of October and November. However, no matter how tamed with ropes and anchors Ama Dablam gets, a fall from its steep slopes is usually lethal.

The upper part of Ama Dablam at sunset. Photo: 8K Expeditions.

Marriage, a Baby, or a Second Income? Change Your W-4 Within Weeks

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (491 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Moneycrashers

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, payroll withholds tax for the household your W-4 describes until you hand in a new one.
  • Every paycheck after the change is withheld at the old setting.
  • Each employer withholds based only on its own paycheck and what your W-4 tells it, such as your filing status and children.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, payroll withholds tax for the household your W-4 describes until you hand in a new one. Within weeks of a wedding, a divorce, a new baby, a second job, or new side income, run the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator. Give your employer the new W-4 it fills in while enough paychecks remain to spread the correction.

Every paycheck after the change is withheld at the old setting. The gap grows each payday, and the paydays left to close it shrink.

Each employer withholds based only on its own paycheck and what your W-4 tells it, such as your filing status and children. So a spouse’s pay, a second job, or side income on your return calls for more withholding. A divorce final by December 31 usually does too, since you’ll be taxed as unmarried for the whole year while payroll still withholds as married. A new child, or a spouse with no income, lets you have less withheld.

Run the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator with your latest pay stub. It counts the new deductions for tips, overtime, seniors, and car loan interest, then fills in a new W-4 that payroll has about a month to start using. When a change like a divorce or a second job leaves you short for the year, the IRS requires the new form within 10 days.

According to recent reports, say newlyweds earn $60,000 each, are paid every two weeks, have no other income, and take the standard deduction. Both switch to married filing jointly in January and skip Step 2, the two-jobs step. Each employer gives its paycheck the couple’s whole standard deduction and lowest brackets, so by our math they end the year about $4,400 short. Fix it in July, and each spouse’s 13 remaining paychecks need about $170 more withheld apiece. Wait until October, and each spouse’s last six need about $360 apiece.

Industry observers note that side income from freelance or gig work has nothing withheld. Extra withholding in Step 4(c) can cover its tax, and when that’s more than your paychecks can spare, pay the rest in quarterly estimated payments. The IRS’s penalty rules count withholding as paid evenly through the year, so raising it in the fall also covers spring’s due dates, which a late estimated payment can’t.

Then rerun the estimator in late December, as the IRS advises, so a catch-up amount sized for a few paychecks doesn’t over-withhold all of next year.

College students have a lot on their plate already, including the need to study to get good grades, participating in any number of on-campus activities and potentially working part-time to have some spending money.

That noted, college students should also focus on their financial future, including steps they can take to build credit before they enter the workforce.

After all, having a credit history and a good credit score can mean being able to rent an apartment, finance a car or take out a loan, whereas having no credit at all can mean sitting on the sidelines until the situation changes.

Industry observers note that fortunately, there are all kinds of ways for young adults to build credit while they’re still in school. Some strategies require a little work on their part, but many are hands-off tasks that you only have to do once.

It has been revealed that make sure your student knows the basic cornerstones of credit building, including the factors that are used to determine credit scores. While factors like new credit, length of credit history and credit mix will play a role in their credit later on, the two most important complications for credit newcomers to focus on include payment history and credit utilization.

Payment history makes up 35% of FICO scores and credit utilization ratio makes up 30% of scores.

Generally speaking, college students and everyone else can score well in these categories by making all bill payments on time and keeping debt levels low. How low?

Industry observers note that most experts recommend keeping credit utilization below 30% at a maximum and below 10% for the best possible results. This means trying to owe less than $300 for every $1,000 in available credit limits at a maximum, but preferably less than $100 for every $1,000 in credit limits.

Sources indicate that one step you can personally take to help a child build credit is adding them to your credit card account as an authorized user. This means they will get a credit card in their name and access to your spending limit, but you are legally responsible for any charges they make. Obviously, this move works best when you have excellent credit and a strong history of on-time payments and you blueprint to continue using credit responsibly .

While this step can be risky if you’re worried your college student will use their card to overspend, you don’t actually have to give them their physical authorized user credit card.

Industry observers note that in fact, they can get credit for your on-time payments whether they have access to a card or not. If you do decide to give them their credit card, you can do so with the agreement they can only use it for emergency expenses.

Industry observers note that your child can build credit faster if they apply for a credit card and get approved for one on their own, yet this can be difficult for students who have no credit history. That remarked, secured credit cards require a refundable cash deposit as collateral are very easy to get approved for.

According to recent reports, some secured credit cards like the Ambition Card by College Ave even offer cash back1 on every purchase and don’t charge interest2. If your child opts to start building credit with a secured credit card, make sure they understand the best ways to build credit quickly — keeping credit utilization low and paying bills early or on time each month.

While secured credit cards are a good option for students with little to no credit get started on their journey to good credit, there are also credit cards specifically designed for college students. Student credit cards are unsecured cards, meaning they don’t require an upfront cash deposit as collateral, but charge interest on any purchases not paid in full each month.

According to recent reports, many student credit cards offer rewards for spending with no annual fee required as well, although these cards do tend to come with a high APR. The key to getting the most out of a student credit card is having your dependent use it only for purchases they can afford and paying off the balance in its entirety each billing cycle. After all, sky high interest rates don’t really matter when you never carry a balance from one month to the next.

“One of the safest ways for college student to build their credit by learning valuable money skills.”.

While secured cards and student credit cards help young adults build credit with each bill payment they make, other payments they’re making can also help.

It has been revealed that in fact, using an app like Experian Boost can help them get credit for utility bills they’re paying, subscriptions they pay for and even rent payments they’re making. This app is also free to use, and you only have to set up most bill payments in the app once to have them reported to the credit bureaus.

There are also rent-specific apps and tools students can use to get credit for rent payments, although they come with fees. Examples include websites like Rental Kharma and RentReporters.

The Fair Isaac Corporation (FICO) also notes that students can start building credit with their student loans during school, even if they’re not officially required to make payments until six months after graduation with federal student loans.

Their advice is to make interest-only payments on federal student loans along with payments on any private student loans they have during college in order to start having those payments reported to the credit bureaus as soon as possible.

“Making interest-only payments as a student will not only positively affect your credit history but will also keep the interest from capitalizing and adding to your student loan balance,” the agency writes.

Sources indicate that of course, interest capitalization on loans would only be an problem with private student loans and  Federal Direct Unsubsidized Loans since the U.S. Department of Education pays the interest on Direct Subsidized Loans while you’re in school at least half-time, for six months after you graduate and during periods of deferment.

Sources indicate that college students don’t have to wait until they’re done with school to start building credit for the future, and it makes sense to start building positive credit habits early on regardless. Tools like a credit card can help students on their way, whether they opt for a secured credit card or a student card. Other steps like using credit-building apps can also help, and with little effort on the student’s part or on yours.

Industry observers note that either way, the best time to start building credit was a few years ago, and the second best time is now. You can give your student a leg up on the future by helping them build credit so it’s there when they need it.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that for the second time in just over a month, a violent storm is approaching Nepal and threatening two meters of fresh snow on already overloaded mountains. This fresh setback comes at the height of the trekking season and also affects several climbing teams, including those engaged in alpine-style expeditions in remote areas.

In a recent development, the first storm hit Nepal toward the end of September and abruptly ended the climbing season on Manaslu. Worst of all, it caused an avalanche that killed 16 Base Camp staff on Himlung. The mountain remained open to commercial expeditions despite the accident, and several guided teams are currently launching their summit pushes.

According to recent reports, manaslu Base Camp tents buried under the snow after the September storm in Nepal. Photo: Shiddi Ghising.

Industry observers note that A low-pressure front that formed in the Bay of Bengal has now developed into a deep depression and will turn into a full cyclone tomorrow. It is expected to hit Nepal on Wednesday or Thursday through the end of the week.

The Nepal National Mountain Guides Association, in association with Senior Meteorologist Krishna Bhakta Manandhar, has put out a detailed forecast. They note that clouds spreading out from this system will hit Nepal’s mountains on October 28, especially above 6,500-7,000m in the eastern part of Nepal, including the Khumbu and Kanchenjunga regions. This will spread over the next two days, causing heavy rains throughout Nepal and snow at higher altitudes.

Industry observers note that authorities and local media have urged trekkers and climbers to modify their intends and avoid river areas and high passes. The main concern is for those at the moment in remote areas without InReach, Starlink, or satphones.

According to recent reports, trekkers should check with local agencies, especially those heading for the Annapurna and Manaslu regions. Several passes there were already cut or in poor condition after the previous storm and subsequent floods.

A Russian team in the Kangchenjunga region is acclimatizing to climb 7,710m Jannu. According to their latest report, they proposal to touch 7,000m before attempting their main goal.

Industry observers note that fellow Russians attempting the West Ridge of Everest have retreated to Kathmandu to rest and recover, so they should not be affected. Andrei Vasiliev, Serguey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov, all climbing without supplemental oxygen, are enduring some lung problems. They returned to Base Camp from their second foray up the mountain last Friday, without reaching 7,500m, as they’d hoped.

Industry observers note that after climbing in the Cholu range, Jost Kobusch of Germany and his small team moved to the Manaslu area for the second stage of his acclimatization before attempting Everest solo in winter, also without oxygen and via the West Ridge. However, the poor state of the trails after the recent floods and the approaching cyclone have thwarted his prepares.

“The flood cut our planned path and, according to forecasts, the incoming cyclone will leave up to two meters of snow,” Kobusch told ExplorersWeb from Samagaon, where the team is pondering their options.

#114637. How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

How Unlimited Free Stuff from Amazon Almost Ruined My Retirement

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon.
  • Sources indicate that “Congratulations!
  • I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It all started last winter when I innocently posted a review for a heated vest I had bought on Amazon. I was happy with this fun latest way to beat the winter and wanted to share it with others, so I gave it five stars. But soon after I clicked “Submit”, I got an email from Amazon which said something like,.

Sources indicate that “Congratulations! You’ve been selected to join Amazon Vine for writing helpful reviews!”.

I was already aware of Amazon Vine since I had seen product reviews from other people in the program – typically called “Vine Voices.” The basic idea of this program is that you can order stuff from Amazon for free, as long as you agree to review at least 80% of the things you order.

“Hey, that’s cool”, I thought, “Who doesn’t like free stuff?

Especially since I’ve already been writing product reviews out of the goodness of my heart – why not be rewarded for it?”.

So without giving it much further thought, I clicked “accept” on their terms and conditions and joined the program.

And so began a saga that has taken me on a surprising journey over the past nine months causing me to:.

Recent findings suggest that okay, I’ll admit that there were also some upsides. My original idea was partly to save some money, by getting stuff I genuinely would have bought anyway, in a way that sounded fun. And that did happen – I saved at least a few thousand dollars on tools and materials for my construction business and the MMM-HQ Coworking space, for free. Plus, at least some of the motivation for signing up was to put myself through an experiment so I could write this blog article about it. And if you’re reading this, it looks like that happened too.

But I was still surprised at how powerful the combination of small nudges and incentives from Amazon was able to hijack my frugality instincts –  and get me to do a bunch of work that wasn’t really the best use of my time.

So I figured if we review my journey and break it down with a bit of Behavioral Science, we could all learn a few valuable things by laughing at Mr. Money Mustache’s folly.

Scarcity Brain and the Online Casino Effect.

In a recent development, one of the most interesting books I’ve read in recent years is Michael Easter’s Scarcity Brain. It’s an exploration of the sneaky ways that modern gambling platforms, marketing and social media algorithms are all built upon two weaknesses in our evolutionary programming:.

As I look back now, I realize that I fell straight into those same traps, because the Vine program has all the key properties of a casino or a TikTok feed:.

Sources indicate that but occasionally, there will be genuinely useful things like super nice light fixtures, tools and plumbing parts, an EV charger, and even some clothing. My favorite ridiculous Eagle shirt as featured in the Mustachianism music video was an Amazon Vine find.

As were a whole supply of super-realistic artificial plants, which while tacky in principle, have been amazing for hard-to-water courtyard garden areas at the MMM HQ.

Sources indicate that I also had a lot of fun roping in friends and coworkers from HQ to help and share in the bounty. I let them help me request and review stuff that they wanted, and then they got to keep it. This seemed like a win/win because we shared the work and the fun of laughing at some of the ridiculous products available.

Still, as I went through this experiment this spring and summer and allowed the system to coax me into doing 80 reviews so I could upgrade my account from Vine Silver to Vine Gold*, I noticed something didn’t feel quite right.

Recent findings suggest that I was checking the Vine page every day for scores, even when I didn’t actually need anything. It would usually be a bust, but just often enough, something I actually wanted would come up, and I’d order it before it was too late. Scarcity and unpredictable rewards at work.

Recent findings suggest that then the bounty would come, I’d unpack it and photograph it with assembly-line speed so I could batch-write all the reviews once per week or so. For every review I did, I was spending time I’d rather spend doing something else. And for every questionable item I got, I was creating pollution and trash from its manufacturing and packaging – directly contradicting the main values of my life and my reason for writing this blog. And I saw all of this, yet I kept doing it!

So Was This The Downfall of MMM?

Sources indicate that during the worst of this consumerism bender, things were dire. I was getting packages almost every day and my recycling bin was overflowing with cardboard. My son and my girlfriend started laughing at some of my more frivolous purchases, so I found myself discreetly tucking away the boxes when they were around to evade scrutiny.

But eventually, I moved into a recovery stage. I had been letting this habit continue out of laziness and as a form of procrastination: it’s very easy to order shit online and pretend I’m doing something useful, and much more difficult to get moving to do the things that really make my life enjoyable.

But I’m old enough to know that hitting the running trails and the gym for my daily workouts, and making progress on all my construction projects, and focusing on the computer as a creative tool rather than an entertainment device so I can get stuff done like this blog post, are the things that bring me the most joy.

It has been revealed that admittedly, some of the sucky factors of the Vine program helped make it easier to recover too. For every genuinely useful thing I found like a contractor-grade extension cord, I had to scan through endless screens of trinkets which not only wasted my time but actually pissed me off at their very existence.

I also noticed some of the deliberately reviewer-unfriendly features built into the program which reminded me that we reviewers are definitely just low-wage workers rather than any form of VIP. The search functionality is crap, and there is no way to filter or sort the results, because they want you to have to look through everything and they don’t care about the value of your time.

Recent findings suggest that then there is the hilariously bureaucratic AI-based evaluation system which would occasionally flag my totally tame, factual reviews as “Not meeting our Community Standards” without explaining what the problem was. So I’d have to go in and edit my review, randomly changing a couple of words and maybe some punctuation, and suddenly the AI would be pacified and accept my review. Just dumb.

This is What “Fuck You Money” is For!

In a recent development, it dawned on me that for many people, this is just what “work” looks like. You are given a bunch of tasks and a bunch of rules to follow, in a system you didn’t create and don’t get much say in changing. And then as long as you crank out your TPS Reports without rocking the boat too much, you get your paycheck.

Recent findings suggest that it reminded me of the Uber Driving experiment I did way back in 2017: as soon as I started working as a driver, I could immediately see dozens of improvements that could be made to the system that would make it function better for both drivers and passengers. But since I wasn’t the boss, nobody wanted to hear my ideas.

Sources indicate that experiences like these remind me that while I love hard work and I love learning upcoming things every day, I greatly prefer being the boss. And I’ve gotten pretty damned accustomed to it after 20 years of financial independence, so I see no need to give it up.

It has been revealed that one interesting “gotcha” of the Vine program is that they do keep track of all the free stuff you get and send you a 1099 for its retail value at the end of the year. So it’s not really free, just discounted to whatever your marginal tax rate is (about 25% for me this year). If we peek into my account right now, this is how my 2025 is looking:.

It has been revealed that so I got about $7000 worth of stuff, and could owe up to $1750 of tax on it. In my case, about 75% of it was “sold” to my business for commercial use (construction supplies which I used on jobs or HQ renovations) so it was effectively converted into real income rather than just tax burden. Some of it was stuff I would have bought anyway for my own house which I’ll gladly pay the taxes on. But there is also probably about $1000 of pure nonsense in there as well, for which I’ll owe a tax bill of $250 as penance for my itchy trigger finger on that “Order” button.

In a recent development, thanks to some advice from wise readers in the comments (below), I have since learned that in most cases you can mark down this estimated value by 80% before declaring it – because you have effectively eliminated most of the resale value by opening and reviewing the product. Thus my tax bill will be more like $50 rather than $250. More detail in this Reddit discussion here.

Sources indicate that so here we are today. While I admit that I didn’t explicitly cancel my account, I used the “Keystone Habit” trick to override the temptation to view the Vine page – mapping that browser bookmark to my daily habits list instead, a little chart which I call my “Badassity Tracker”. The net result is that every time I click it, I’m taken straight to a reminder to get up from the computer and do a quick round of exercise, so I do that instead.

Industry observers note that and of course my writing of this article may be a violation of the terms and conditions of the program (“the first rule of Vine is to not talk about Vine”), so it might even get canceled on me. (and if so I’ll let you know because that would be funny story as well).

According to recent reports, but I learned a lot about habits and addiction, and realized that this same feeling might be what drives people into One More Year Syndrome, as they keep working even when they can afford to quit. I have now coached enough people through this situation to see it is way more common than I would have ever guessed.

As with all MMM articles, there’s a real life lesson in this story. It’s not really about Vine or me or my habits, it’s about you continuing to look at yourself and your life, and always questioning your own assumptions or patterns. And asking the people you trust most for feedback as well:.

Sources indicate that we will never be perfect, but the great news is we don’t have to be. All it takes is a little bit of self reflection and putting ourselves on a slightly better path, as often as we can as life goes on. We are all on a very long journey, so even a tiny course correction can make a huge difference in where we end up.

Industry News: Mont Blanc Has Grown Almost Two Meters — But Not in the Way You Think

📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (549 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

💡 Key Takeaways
  • These days, topographic surveys typically show that a mountain’s altitude is decreasing due to shrinking snowcaps.
  • According to recent reports, mont Blanc is now 1.88 meters taller than it was three years ago, according to a recent report by France’s IGN (National Geographic Institute).
  • However, it may be wise to wait before changing the figure in climbing guides.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

These days, topographic surveys typically show that a mountain’s altitude is decreasing due to shrinking snowcaps. But strangely, Mont Blanc, the highest peak in the Alps, has grown significantly since its latest measurement in 2023.

According to recent reports, mont Blanc is now 1.88 meters taller than it was three years ago, according to a recent report by France’s IGN (National Geographic Institute). The new official altitude is now 4,807.47 meters (15,772.5 feet) above sea level.

However, it may be wise to wait before changing the figure in climbing guides. Measurements are carried out every two years, and each time the registered altitude varies:.

Graphic showing the results of the last few measurements on Mont Blanc, by LaChangingMeteo.

Mont Blanc’s “summit is constantly shifting,” Jean des Garets, chief geometer in the Haute-Savoie department, told Le Monde. “Each individual measurement is not significant in itself.”.

So, what’s with the yearly differences? Obviously, it’s the variation in the thick but ever-changing snowcap that covers the summit.

The mountain’s rocky summit measures around 4,792m above sea level. The snow cover varies with the seasons. The difference from the previous measurement reveals that 2023 was much drier at summit altitude.

It has been revealed that the survey team on itsir way to the summit of Mont Blanc.. Photo: ING.

A team from the Order of Chartered Surveyors (Ordre des géomètres-experts) acclimatized first by climbing Bishorn (4,153m). They then spent some days measuring several points around the mountain. Finally, they climbed Mont Blanc via the normal route on September 15-16.

Once on top, they pinpointed the highest point using a GNSS (Global Navigation Satellite System) pole, which measures altitude in real time.

The recent survey featured an interesting novelty. In addition to altitude, the survey also measured Mont Blanc’s gravity by installing a gravimeter on the summit for the first time ever. This measured the force with which the Earth attracts the device. In so doing, they wanted to determine whether the summit has sunk, regardless of ice cover.

Recent findings suggest that the gravimeter on the summit of Mont Blanc, September 16. Photo: ING France.

“When the height of Mont Blanc changes, we can’t know for sure whether the ground or the rock has moved or if the ice has melted,” explains Olivier Jamet.

Sources indicate that gravity provides the missing information: mass. If the ice has melted, there is less material under the instrument, but the rock has moved closer to it. Distinguishing these two effects requires a model of the ice cap and the massif, and above all, repeated measurements at the same location. And the effort is worthwhile, especially now that the effects of climate change on Alpine glaciers are becoming increasingly apparent.

The gravimeter on the top of Mont Blanc measured the gravity at 9.7944689 m/s².

“For comparison, this value is 9.81 m/s² in Marseille (located at sea level) and 9.8043046 m/s² in Saint-Gervais-Le Fayet (580m above sea level),” ING reports. “This difference in value, even if it seems small, allows for the detection of changes in mass, particularly in the mass of the ice. Repeated over time, these gravity measurements will thus contribute to improving the determination of the altitude of the highest peak in Western Europe.”.

  • A luxury retinol night cream that lists 0.3% retinol costs $160 an ounce.
  • Choosing a drugstore serum over the cream saves $120 to $130 an ounce, and the cream’s higher price doesn’t guarantee better results.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Skin care results come from a short list of proven ingredients, like retinoids, vitamin C, and sunscreen, not from the price. Drugstore brands sell them, often for a fraction of luxury prices. Before you buy, check the label for the active ingredient and its strength, then pick the cheapest product that lists both.

A luxury retinol night cream that lists 0.3% retinol costs $160 an ounce. Drugstore night serums with the same 0.3% retinol cost $30 to $40 an ounce.

Choosing a drugstore serum over the cream saves $120 to $130 an ounce, and the cream’s higher price doesn’t guarantee better results. The American Academy of Dermatology notes products that work come at every price, and its dermatologists rank sunscreen and moisturizer as the two most effective anti-aging buys.

Recent findings suggest that beyond those two, choose products by their active ingredient. In a 2025 study in the Journal of the American Academy of Dermatology, dermatologists narrowed 318 skin care ingredients to 23 they agree on for problems like wrinkles, acne, and dark spots.

In a recent development, three of the 23 are drugstore staples. Match the one on the label to what you want to fix:.

Over-the-counter retinol products don’t have to state their strength on the label, so choose one that does and start with the lowest strength you can find. For any of the three, compare products by the ingredient and its strength, not the jar or the scent, and buy the cheapest one that matches. Makeup is a separate question, since how it looks on you is part of what you pay for.

Sources indicate that keep the daily routine to a cleanser, a moisturizer, and a sunscreen labeled broad-spectrum with SPF 30 or higher. A moisturizer with the same label counts as both. After a few weeks, add one active ingredient for the concern that bothers you most, since starting several at once can irritate your skin. Deep, painful acne or acne that scars needs a dermatologist from the start, because store-bought products are unlikely to clear it.

Give each latest active ingredient at least six weeks, and if three months pass with no change, see a board-certified dermatologist instead of buying a pricier product.

Pick the market by its numbers, hire a local agent, inspector, and property manager before you offer, and see the house on live video or in person before closing.

What you’d learn on a visit, from the roof’s condition to the for-rent signs on the block, has to come from numbers you can check and people you hire.

Look for a city that’s adding jobs and residents. The Bureau of Labor Statistics’ Economy at a Glance tables track its metro area’s jobs, and Census QuickFacts tracks its population. Compare a year’s rent with the price, the test that picks out cities where rent still covers the mortgage. Read the state’s landlord-tenant law on deposits and evictions.

According to recent reports, then hire your local team before you make an offer, the property manager first, since a good one knows which blocks keep tenants. Say an investor in San Jose likes a $190,000 house in Indianapolis that would rent for $1,650 a month. The manager she hires first warns her that houses on that block sit empty for months between tenants and steers her to a house two streets over.

According to recent reports, interview managers the way you’d interview a job candidate. Call owners whose rentals they manage, and check any license the state requires. Add an agent who works with investors and knows what nearby houses rent for, an independent inspector you hire yourself, and a mortgage lender that will finance a rental in that state. A turnkey rental, one a organization has already renovated and rented, calls for checks of its own.

Industry observers note that for each house, find out the property tax a rental would owe and get a landlord insurance quote. The Government Accountability Office found that average homeowners insurance premiums in southern coastal areas rose at least 25% from 2019 to 2024, against 3% nationwide.

Sources indicate that have your agent walk you through the house on a live video call before you offer. Write the offer with an inspection contingency, which lets you renegotiate or back out if the inspection turns up problems.

Set aside cash for whatever the inspector flagged and the rest of the first year’s repairs, and visit before closing or soon after to meet your manager and see the house.

In April, Robert Cowden, 52, set off on foot from New Haven, Kansas, on a two-stage journey across the United States. First, he planned to walk nearly 2,000km to Pittsburgh, then canoe 3,200km downriver to the Gulf of Mexico. With him is his dog, Enzo, a pointer-mix.

Robert Cowden and Enzo. Photo: Enzo The Great: An American Expedition.

According to recent reports, when he left Upcoming Haven with Enzo, Cowden was at a low point. His battle with alcohol addiction had cost him his job, car, and home. Entering a residential treatment program would leave Enzo with no place to go. Now sober and with housing waiting for him after the end of his journey, Cowden sees his expedition as part of the larger effort to rebuild his life.

Sources indicate that during the walking stage, Cowden towed his camping gear and supplies in a cart, which Enzo could ride in to take a break from walking. Setting out with very little, Cowden has relied on the kindness of strangers, both online and on the trail, to continue his expedition.

Sources indicate that “The number one warning you’re going to get on a walk across America is, ‘Be careful, there’s creepy people and bad people,'” Cowden recalled, speaking to a local KOMU 8 reporter while passing through Missouri. Instead, he’s been overwhelmingly met with generosity and helpfulness.

Cowden highlights the wear on his trail shoes, as Enzo looks on. Photo: Enzo The Great: An American Expedition.

Industry observers note that cowden completed the walking stage in September. Now, he’s on the Ohio River and hopes to reach the Gulf by the end of 2026. While the second stage lets him and Enzo get off their feet, it has its own challenges. They rolled out the canoe into the Allegheny River at Pittsburgh. It soon joined the Ohio, and lengthy stretches of slow water pushed Cowden to paddle continuously.

Sources indicate that it’s 1,579km down the Ohio to its confluence with the Mississippi in Illinois, which Cowden and Enzo aim to complete in under 40 days. They’re currently on pace, averaging about 20km a day.

Cowden posts regular updates on Facebook and on the expedition’s webpage.

  • The pink tax is the extra charged for a product marketed to women when it differs from the men’s version only in color, scent, or packaging.
  • According to recent reports, when New York City’s Department of Consumer Affairs compared nearly 800 products sold in men’s and women’s versions in 2015, the women’s versions cost 7% more on average and 13% more for personal care.
  • In a 2018 study of 10 personal care categories, the Government Accountability Office found women’s versions cost more in five, deodorant among them, but men’s cost more for shaving gel and nondisposable razors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The pink tax is the extra charged for a product marketed to women when it differs from the men’s version only in color, scent, or packaging. Compare the price per ounce or per item of both versions, check that the ingredients match, and buy the cheaper one, whichever aisle you find it in.

According to recent reports, when New York City’s Department of Consumer Affairs compared nearly 800 products sold in men’s and women’s versions in 2015, the women’s versions cost 7% more on average and 13% more for personal care. The widest gap was hair care, where women paid 48% more than men for shampoo and conditioner.

In a 2018 study of 10 personal care categories, the Government Accountability Office found women’s versions cost more in five, deodorant among them, but men’s cost more for shaving gel and nondisposable razors.

Some of the difference in the city’s study came from package size. It found men’s deodorant often sold in 2.7-ounce sticks and women’s in 2.6-ounce sticks at the same price, so compare the unit price, the cost per ounce or per item.

Say a pink four-pack of disposable razors costs $6 and the same razor in a blue six-pack costs $7.50. That’s $1.50 a razor against $1.25, so the blue pack is the cheaper buy. Then make sure the formulas match. For an antiperspirant, compare the active ingredient and strength on the Drug Facts label. For a shampoo, compare the first several ingredients, which are listed in order of amount.

In California and New York, a business can’t charge different prices for substantially similar products or services based on gender. A haircut or a dry-cleaning job can still cost more when it takes more time or skill. California’s Gender Tax Repeal Act also makes barbers, salons, tailors, and dry cleaners post prices for their standard services, and New York entitles you to a written price list on request from any service business.

Report a product priced by gender to California’s attorney general. In New York, file a complaint with the Division of Consumer Protection to seek back the difference you paid, or call its helpline at 1-800-697-1220.

Start with deodorant, the category both studies found pricier for women than for men, and compare the price per ounce of a men’s or unisex stick with the same active ingredient and strength.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Measure your pet’s meals with a kitchen scale or a level measuring cup, and feed the label’s amount for the weight your pet should be, not its current weight. Count treats as part of the day’s food. Eyeballed portions tend to run major, so the bag empties sooner and the extra pounds raise vet bills.

Those extra pounds are common. In the Association for Pet Obesity Prevention’s 2022 survey, veterinary professionals found 59% of dogs and 61% of cats overweight or obese.

Even a cup or scoop leaves room for error. When University of Guelph researchers had 100 dog owners measure set amounts of kibble, their portions ran from 48% too little to 152% too much, and the smallest amount, a quarter cup, gave them the most trouble.

Say the feeding chart calls for a third of a cup a day and your cat gets half a cup. That’s 50% more than the chart’s amount, so a bag meant to last two months is gone in about six weeks and your cost per day rises by the same 50%. The American Animal Hospital Association’s nutrition guidelines link obesity to arthritis and diabetes. In Banfield Pet Hospital’s 2017 report, owners of overweight dogs spent 17% more on health care and 25% more on medications than owners of healthy-weight dogs.

In a recent development, weigh meals on a kitchen scale, which the same guidelines rate as more accurate than measuring cups. Weigh one level cup of the food once, and a third-cup meal is a third of that weight. With a cup, pick one the size of the portion and level it off.

It has been revealed that use the chart’s amount for your pet’s ideal weight, which your vet can tell you, and treat it as a starting point. The guidelines base a pet’s calories on its ideal weight and warn that the amounts on labels can run high.

Keep treats to 10% of the day’s calories, the guidelines’ limit, or use pieces of the day’s measured kibble as treats. A bowl that stays full all day can’t be measured, so switch to set meals.

Industry observers note that then check your pet’s shape. You should be able to feel its ribs but not see them, and see a waist behind them from above. If you have to press to find the ribs, feed a little less, whatever the chart says.
